author: Unknown
title: Gli USA, l’eterogenesi dei fini della globalizzazione e l’illusione della sfera di influenza atlantica
content:
Tre domande a Mimmo Porcaro, ripubblichiamo da

Sinistra in Rete


Alberto Deambrogio: Mimmo Porcaro, tu sostieni che gli USA non possono fare a meno di pensarsi su uno scenario globale per fare fronte al loro tipo di economia, nonostante la crisi della globalizzazione da loro voluta. Oggi vediamo all’ opera l’eterogenesi dei fini e la stessa tregua con l’Iran mostra come gli sviluppi di questa crisi siano largamente indefiniti. Tu che ne pensi?


Mimmo Porcaro

: Il problema è proprio quello dell’impulso irrefrenabile del capitalismo all’espansione globale del suo raggio d’azione. Un’espansione (resa necessaria dal bisogno di valorizzare una massa crescente di capitale) che comporta per gli Usa non certo il dominio diretto dei territori altrui (troppo costoso), ma la diffusione di centinaia di basi militari in quasi tutto il mondo: perché la minaccia militare, e la guerra contro ogni tipo di stato che intenda far valere dei confini o comunque non accettare passivamente l’espansione, sono l’accompagnamento necessario degli investimenti Usa all’estero. E sono, inoltre, la tutela più forte del ruolo del dollaro, essenziale alla gestione del debito di Washington. Si chiama 

imperialismo

, ed è importante capirlo perché “imperialismo” significa che la tendenza alla guerra è oggettiva, è inscritta nell’economia capitalistica e non nello stato in quanto tale, e segnerà un’epoca intera.


Quanto sopra va ricordato sia a coloro che sperano di tornare alla globalizzazione, come se questa fosse stata il trionfo delle “pacifiche” reti economico-sociali su un’ “antiquata” logica statale, sia a quelli che credono che si possa in qualche modo tornare a una divisione in sfere di influenza, e che Trump, con tutto il male che se ne può dire, sia comunque uno che lavora a un nuovo equilibrio. In realtà la globalizzazione è stata una forma dell’imperialismo, particolarmente adeguata al momento unipolare Usa. Non a caso è stata accompagnata da una vera e propria sequela di guerre (Serbia, Irak, Afghanistan, Libia…) che hanno sancito il “diritto” degli Usa di sparare 

ad libitum

.


Non a caso è stata pensata e gestita anche come un altro modo per fronteggiare la rinascita della Germania e del Giappone, svanita l’Urss, attraverso l’uso dell’economia come sostituto della guerra (investimenti condizionanti, trattamento preferenziale per le imprese Usa, dazi – ben prima di Trump – politiche fiscali aggressive, ecc.). Quanto alle zone d’influenza, ogni volta che qualche decisore o qualche 

think tank

nordamericano descrive quella che potrebbe/dovrebbe essere la zona d’influenza Usa, quest’ultima tende ad assomigliare pericolosamente al monto intero, o quanto meno a due terzi di esso. Ciò non vuol dire che gli Usa non possano scegliere, per fasi più o meno lunghe, una sorta di 

retrenchment

, ossia una limitazione del campo d’azione e un “trinceramento” nella zona atlantica. Ma: a) ciò, quando avviene anche solo in parte, comporta grossi guai per la suddetta zona (chiedere a Venezuela, Cuba, sinistre latinoamericane, Danimarca…e Nato); e b) ciò limiterebbe espansione e profitti, con serie conseguenze per la tenuta interna e nuove spinte alla proiezione esterna per risolvere i guai di casa. Comunque, va detto subito, questo non è il caso di Trump, o comunque è solo un aspetto della sua azione. Trump regola i conti nella sfera atlantica non per restarvi confinato, ma per meglio colpire Xi. La guerra all’Iran, è – per convinzione, per ricatto israeliano, per il peso degli apparati e delle esigenze oggettive che essi segnalano, o magari per un mix di tutto ciò – la prosecuzione di una strategia anticinese, concepita ai tempi di Biden, che consiste nello sconfiggere o indebolire uno per uno i principali alleati di Pechino (Mosca e Teheran) per poi liberare forze dal fronte euro/mediorientale e volgerle contro il nemico principale. E, preso atto dell’impasse dell’ “operazione Ucraina”, la sconfitta dell’Iran avrebbe consentito il disimpegno quantomeno da quel quadrante geopolitico (come ha ben spiegato Salvatore Minolfi, attento studioso della politica estera Usa : 

https://www.lafionda.org/2026/06/08/sequencing-e-disperazione-strategica/

). Scelta fallimentare: anche da ciò l’ulteriore pressione sui paesi europei per un maggiore e più autonomo impegno antirusso.

author: Rein Tarinay
title: Filipinos in Toronto denounce Marcos Jr’s SONA
content:
TORONTO – “Marcos Jr., mahiya ka naman.”

Filipino progressive groups and solidarity allies held a People’s State of the Nation Address (PSONA) in Toronto’s Little Manila in response to the administration’s State of the Nation Address. The groups called for the rejection of the Marcos regime, as well as the ongoing imperialist war and plunder.

“The Marcos family is a reflection of political dynasty families like the Dutertes who continue to enjoy their power and wealth while the vast majority of Filipinos suffer. BBM said nothing of the 62 million Filipinos struggling with incomes under P22,000 or Can$500 (Canadian dollar) monthly, while the richest 0.1 percent have over P17 million or almost Can$400,000 monthly,” said Kim Garcia, coordinator of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Toronto.

“Marcos Jr. mahiya ka naman!” Apol Apuntar of TAMA NA Coalition Toronto, a coalition against corruption. Apuntar criticized Marcos Jr.’s announcement of amnesty on estate taxes as the Marcos family has neither paid the billions of taxes they owe the Philippine government nor returned the wealth they plundered.

The groups also destroyed effigies of Marcos Jr., Vice President Sara Duterte, and Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa. They also tore down cardboard images of US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, as well as Marcos Jr.

The action symbolized the impact of US and Canadian imperialism, as well as Marcos Jr.’s subservience to foreign interests. (DAA)

author: Susan Price
title: Ecology and imperialism
content:
Ana Cristina Carvalhaes is a founding member of Brazil’s Socialism and Liberty Party. In this interview with Green Left ’s Federico Fuentes , Carvalhaes argues for a non-dogmatic theory of imperialism that incorporates ecology.

Imperialism is a Marxist concept, though the word is commonly used in the media and by non-Marxist scholars.

The answer to your questions depends on the Marxist perspective you analyse it from, as there are various forms of Marxism. I subscribe to one that rejects immutable dogmas, untouchable classics and sanctified gurus.

Such ahistorical views contradict the essence of Marxist historical materialism.

Imperialism remains extremely valid and useful today, even if it has been enriched by reality and new phenomena in the 110 years since Lenin ’ s seminal pamphlet on the topic .

I am among those who defend and draw upon the concept of imperialism, formulated and debated by a great generation of Marxists at the turn of the 20th century.

But I also think we must draw on the history of these past 100-plus years, and on important contributions regarding new phenomena in the global economy and geopolitics, especially by activists and theorists from the so-called Global South.

What elements of Lenin’s pamphlet have been superseded by subsequent developments?

The merit of Lenin’s synthesis lies, above all, in that it revealed an extraordinary long-term strategic vision.

As a revolutionary, Lenin was concerned about the war, which had already claimed hundreds of thousands of lives in Europe when the pamphlet was written in 1916, and how socialists on both sides of the trenches should respond.

Most of what he described as imperialism remains relevant today:

• the systemic predominance of an alliance between banking capital and industrial capital — finance capital;

• the growing tendency towards capital’s concentration through the formation of monopolies or oligopolies — the end of free competition;

• the ever-widening development gap between core and non-core countries;

• the tendency of industrialised nations, driven by capital’s needs, to expand their political, military and economic power over others; and

• rivalry among imperialist powers and the tendency toward war.

Each characteristic aptly describes today’s crises — with the notable exception of the ecological and climate crisis.

Broadly speaking, the Marxist theory of imperialism has proven correct in the long run, though, of course, not without shortcomings.

The Marxist theory of imperialism, further developed by Latin American dependency theorists and anti-colonial thinkers from Africa and Asia, rightly emphasises the core-periphery contradiction.

But it took a long time to recognise the emergence of intermediate state-economies. These state-economies are dependent on core imperialist powers, but oppress neighbours and partners at the regional level.

They do not quite qualify as part of the core, but are no longer simply periphery. Brazil is one case. This group is highly heterogeneous due to historic, social and demographic differences, among others.

Second, but no less important, is that no attention was paid to industrial capitalism’s predatory impacts on nature. In fact, nature did not appear in the writings of these thinkers.

They failed, for example, to elaborate on the link between imperialism and inequalities in terms of the far greater environmental destruction inflicted on the colonised.

How important is the integration of the environmental crisis into our understanding of imperialism?

This belated incorporation is, in my view, the most important contribution to Marxist theory since the 1970s.

There is an expanding body of work on the subject, one that has grown in line with the rising number of ecological disasters, increasing awareness among broad sections of society, and mounting evidence of the climate and biodiversity crises we face.

The main Marxist and Marxist-influenced theorists contributing to this ongoing discussion include Michael Löwy, Ian Angus, James O’Connor, Daniel Bensaïd, John Bellamy Foster, Jason Moore, Ariel Salleh, Andreas Malm, Maristella Svampa and Kohei Saito.

Anti-capitalists, such as Naomi Klein, have been crucial to popularising the issue.

The incorporation of ecology by Marxist theorists and social movements was — and remains — essential, as combating capitalism is a matter of human survival.

This system destroys nature. If the capitalist system — which gave rise to …

author: Unknown
title: A Vietnam in the Field of Culture: The Cultural Congress of Havana, 1968
content:
The collages in this dossier were created by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research based on images and speeches from the 1968 Cultural Congress of Havana, courtesy of Cubarte.


‘There can be nothing more anti-Marxist than dogma… nothing more anti-Marxist than the petrification of ideas’.


– Fidel Castro, closing speech, Cultural Congress of Havana, 12 January 1968

1


‘I make revolution, therefore I exist, therefore we exist’.


– René Depestre, commission I, Cultural Congress of Havana, 1968

2


On the morning of 4 January 1968, in the Hotel Habana Libre, Cuban president Osvaldo Dorticós opened the Cultural Congress of Havana. Over the following 9 days, 470 delegates from 70 countries would fill the commission rooms. Together, they sought to understand how imperialism operates through culture in all its dimensions and what it would mean to build an anti-imperialist front capable of confronting and dismantling it.

3


The congress took place at a moment when revolution felt not only possible but imminent. Vietnam was fighting the most powerful military on Earth to a standstill. Armed liberation movements in the Portuguese colonies of Angola, Guinea-Bissau, and Mozambique were building new societies in the zones they had already liberated.

4

 Across Latin America, guerrilla movements were multiplying in the wake of the Cuban Revolution. The peoples of the Third World were in motion on every front. The grief over Ernesto ‘Che’ Guevara’s murder in Bolivia three months earlier had only sharpened the collective resolve of the delegates and the movements they represented. The question was no longer whether imperialism could be defeated but by whom and on what fronts.


The Cultural Congress of Havana was organised across five commissions that mapped the fronts on which the cultural battle was being waged: Culture and National Independence (commission I); the Integral Formation of Man (commission II); the Responsibility of the Intellectual (commission III); Culture and Mass Media (commission IV); and Artistic Creation and Scientific-Technical Work (commission V).

5

 As Dorticós observed in his opening statement, it was ‘the first time, as far as we know, [that people] from all continents, belonging to different professions’ had been brought together around a common cultural mandate.

6

 The decision to invite not only cultural workers such as artists and writers but also doctors, economists, sociologists, scientists, technicians, and intellectual workers of all backgrounds was a deliberate political choice, insisting that culture was not merely an auxiliary to political and military struggle but a front of anti-imperialist struggle in its own right.


The congress was not confined to commission rooms and speeches: it reverberated across the city through billboards, posters, and radio broadcasts. In the lead-up to the congress, the Instituto del Libro (Institute of the Book) published popular editions of works by several participating writers, and films by some of the delegates were screened in cinemas across Havana. On the evening of 9 January, the exhibition

Del Tercer Mundo

 (From the Third World) opened at the Pabellón Cuba in Vedado. Conceived as a cinematic journey rather than a conventional exhibition, it used light, sound, montage, and movement to guide visitors through the unfinished history of Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Visitors moved through six zones that told the unfinished story of the Third World, from the myth of ‘virgin’ lands, through the violence and deprivation of imperial domination, and to the revolutionary struggles of the present. The exhibition drew on neon animations, comic strips, satirical film montage, and sound effects that included a horror tunnel of hunger and rotating light boxes that multiplied Cuban photographer Alberto Korda’s iconic image of Che alongside the question: ‘And we, the exploited of the world, what is our role?’ The exhibition, produced collectively by over a hundred people, was visited by more than 250,000 during its three-month run, with hours that allowed students and workers to attend on their way home, as if visiting a popular cinema.

7


The mass participation and cultural breadth of the congress embodied its foundational argument: that culture contains the totality of how a society produces and reproduces human life. As the congress’s general declaration concluded: ‘if the defeat of imperialism is the unavoidable prerequisite for the …

author: ROAPE
title: Burkina Faso and the return of political economy
content:
Contemporary global political discourses are often noted for their intense polarization, in which elections are increasingly reduced from choices about governance and ideology to something more banal and ritualistic. They are fought over culture, identity, migration, values, and symbols. One of the emblematic “achievements” of the neoliberal order has been the systematic removal of political economy from the sphere of democratic concern, contestation, and participation. Citizens are encouraged to discuss almost everything except capital and economic power, ownership, resources, and production.


The significance of Burkina Faso’s recent political trajectory – and that of Sahelian states such as Mali and Niger – lies not simply in

military coups

 or the charismatic figure of Ibrahim Traoré. It is instead inherent in challenging what political systems across the globe have sought to depoliticize: Who owns national resources? Who benefits from them? What is economic sovereignty, and how is it related to political sovereignty and nation-building?


The depoliticization of political economy is neither accidental nor merely abstract. One of the central assumptions of neoliberalism and its economic precursors has been that markets are neutral, non-political, and objective arbiters of economic life. Economic decision-making – from the allocation of resources to their distribution – is increasingly relegated to ‘specialists’. As economic historian Clara Mattei has shown in

The Capital Order

, austerity emerged not as a neutral economic response but as a political project aimed at containing popular demands. Modern economics similarly tends to treat privatisation and resource allocation as technical rather than political questions, removing them from democratic scrutiny and public control.


Within this framework, debt is increasingly presented as an economic necessity rather than a political choice. This tendency has been especially visible in discussions of Africa’s political economy, where European dependence on African mineral wealth is often obscured beneath the language of equal exchange between sovereign states. Such arrangements compromise sovereignty through the maintenance of comprador elites and economic structures that privilege external interests. Political participation – both in the West and in many African states – thus, increasingly concerns consumption, preferences, and recognition rather than extraction, labour, ownership, and production. Citizens remain politically visible as consumers but increasingly invisible as producers.


The politics of Burkina Faso has challenged this order. From Thomas Sankara’s insistence that political independence without economic sovereignty is incomplete to contemporary debates over mining and resource control, the central issue remains the same: who governs the material foundations of collective national life? In this framing, the

laissez-faire

 assumption is challenged by restoring primacy to the political question.


In my

recent article

,

Military Marxism and Africa’s Community-to-Come

, I argue – with Adam Mayer’s recent work on Military Marxism at the centre – that one of the defining features of contemporary political developments in Burkina Faso is precisely this return of political economy to the sphere of democratic and popular contestation. The ownership of gold mines, the terms under which foreign companies extract resources, the relationship between national wealth and national development, and the broader question of who exercises effective sovereignty over the economy have once again become objects of public debate and ground-level political mobilization.


Consider the question of mining. For decades, debates surrounding African mineral wealth have often been framed in technical terms: investment climates, regulatory frameworks, market efficiency, contractual stability, and foreign direct investment. These concerns are not unimportant. Yet such language frequently obscures a more fundamental political question: who benefits from the extraction of national resources? In Burkina Faso, this question has increasingly been posed not as a technical matter for economists, development agencies, or international financial institutions, but as a question of sovereignty. The issue is no longer simply whether resources are extracted efficiently, but whether the structures governing extraction reflect the priorities of the Burkinabè people.


This development is …

author: ROAPE
title: The homophobia of Pan-African regimes
content:
West Africa has experienced a series of significant geopolitical developments in recent years, with the potential to reshape both its political landscape and economic trajectory. These are, in many ways, years in which decades have passed. Longstanding regimes have collapsed, populations have expanded rapidly, and economic growth has, in aggregate terms, generally trended upwards across the region. Yet these positive developments have been accompanied by equally serious challenges. A persistent jihadist insurgency continues to destabilise the Sahel, military coups have undermined the post-90s move towards democratisation, and regional institutions such as ECOWAS have seen their legitimacy increasingly questioned, particularly in light of the emergence of the

Alliance of Sahel States

 as a contender to the Pan-African aspiration of politically uniting the region.


An increased repression of LGBT+ communities


Among these developments, one particularly alarming trend, and the focus of this submission, concerns the resurgence of legislative and political repression targeting gender and sexual minorities. Recent developments in Burkina Faso and Mali illustrate the severity of this trend. In Burkina Faso, the military government under

Captain Ibrahim Traoré

 introduced legislation imposing a maximum 5-year prison sentence for homosexuality. This was later unanimously passed by his transitional assembly, materially jeopardising the social acceptance and relative safety of a country where LGBT Burkinabés had previously lived without fear of imprisonment (The Guardian, 2025). This change followed a similar law announced by the military government of neighbouring Mali, which also banned same-sex relationships and introduced mandatory 2-7 year prison sentences for an entire community of people, supposedly in the name of defending ‘traditional and moral values’ (Kojoué, 2024).


These developments, while alarming, are not entirely surprising when situated within the broader political context. Both regimes have simultaneously overseen restrictions on political and civil liberties such as the right of public assembly, alongside crackdowns on journalists and dissidents (Hughes, 2025). However, these actions must not be divorced from the context of the ongoing deadly Sahel insurgency as well as the structural economic constraints associated with longstanding patterns of dependency – i.e. Françafrique. As I have outlined elsewhere, if extremism is to be understood as a germ, poverty is the condition that allows said germ to spread rapidly (Doucouré 2024), with said poverty being directly attributable to the persistence of uneven trade dependencies and extractive commerce rooted in colonialism. It is no coincidence that in two of the poorest and most economically exploited nations of our planet, we may observe serious political instability, the rise of military rule, and extremism. With that said, it would be analytically insufficient to attribute the rise in

the persecution of gender and sexual minorities

 solely to military governance or neocolonial pressures. Indeed, the Republic of Senegal offers an intriguing and instructive mini-case study through which we may complicate the easy answers to questions to be asked of this trend. This is a country that, per Regional/Central bank data, attained for its citizens over 85% of the GDP per capita of both Burkina Faso and Mali, combined. Although, like many emerging economies, the material reality of this relatively strong economic performance is deeply uneven, with poverty very much remaining a significant issue in Senegal.


Concerning the rise in homophobic repression across West Africa, Senegal is a useful case study to consider here not primarily because of its economic position relative to Burkina Faso and Mali but, rather, because the country has generally been praised by geopolitical observers for having preserved a ‘democratic tradition’ (Center for Strategic and International Studies,2024); the transfer of power from civilian to civilian has persisted in spite of domestic and numerous regional constitutional crises (Yabi and Holman, 2024). The country has never experienced a single coup d’etat, a matter of significance given that the fact that Africa as a whole has experienced, until 2010, at least 169 coup attempts – with 51.5% ultimately being successful seizures of power (Powell and Thyne 2011, p. 255).


These democratic and constitutional credentials are to be …

title: ‘Mesele sadece bina yenilemek değil, kentsel bütünlük’
content:
17 Ağustos 1999 gecesi meydana gelen 7.4 büyüklüğündeki Kocaeli-Gölcük merkezli deprem, Türkiye tarihinin en büyük yıkımlarından biri olarak kayıtlara geçti. 45 saniye süren sarsıntı, resmi verilere göre 18 binden fazla kişinin ölümüne, on binlerce yaralanmaya ve yaklaşık 300 bin yapının ağır veya orta derecede hasar görmesine neden oldu. İstanbul’da özellikle Avcılar, Küçükçekmece ve Bağcılar gibi bölgelerde yaşanan ağır yıkımlar ve can kayıpları, fay hattından öte yapı niteliği, zemin yapısı ve kentsel planlamanın hayati önemini ortaya koydu.

Aradan geçen 27 yılda İstanbul’u beklenen Marmara depremine hazırlamak amacıyla yürütüldüğü söylenen kentsel dönüşüm çalışmaları ise hız kazandı. Ancak dönüşümün kenti afete ne ölçüde hazırladığı tartışma konusu olmaya devam ediyor. Şehir Plancıları Odası (ŞPO) 2. Başkanı Özgürgün Gürbüz, İstanbul’da yürütülen kentsel dönüşüm projelerini, bu projelerin denetim süreçlerini ve altyapı kapasitesini değerlendirdi.

Kentsel dönüşüm ile deprem riskinin azaltılmasının aynı şey olarak görülmemesi gerektiğini belirten Özgürgün Gürbüz, riskli yapıların yenilenmesinin hazırlığın yalnızca bir parçası olduğunu vurguladı. Deprem riskinin, tek tek yapıların dayanıklılığından çok daha geniş bir kentsel mesele olduğunu söyleyen Gürbüz, “İstanbul’un depreme hazırlanması konusunda 1999’dan bu yana çeşitli çalışmalar yapıldı. 2002 tarihli Japon Uluslararası İş Birliği Ajansı (JICA) çalışması mahalle ölçeğinde bina ve altyapıların hasar görebilirliğini incelemiş, 2003 İstanbul deprem master planı ise yapıların yanı sıra imar uygulamaları, altyapı, finansman, hukuk, eğitim ve afet yönetimi gibi çok sayıda başlığı birlikte ele almıştı. Bugün hâlâ bu çalışmaların işaret ettiği temel sorunların önemli bir bölümünü tartışıyor olmamız, meselenin teknik bilgi eksikliğinden çok uygulama ve koordinasyon sorunu olduğunu gösteriyor” dedi.

Dönüşümün başarısının sadece yenilenen bina sayısıyla ölçülemeyeceğine değinen Gürbüz, “Hangi binaların önceliklendirildiği, yüksek riskli bölgelerde dönüşümün ne hızla ilerlediği, altyapının ve ulaşım sisteminin nasıl güçlendirildiği, nüfus yoğunluğunun nasıl değiştiği ve afet sonrasında kentin nasıl işleyeceğinin birlikte değerlendirilmesi gerekiyor. Aksi halde bina ölçeğinde başarılı görünen ama kent ölçeğinde eksik kalan bir dönüşüm ortaya çıkabilir” ifadelerini kullandı.

Gürbüz, kentsel dönüşüm süreçlerinde verilen destekler açısından geçmişe oranla ciddi artışlar olduğunu söylese de, çelişkili bir durum ortaya çıktığını belirtiyor: “Yarısı bizden kampanyasında hibe, kredi ve tahliye desteğiyle toplam 1 milyon 875 bin TL’lik destek sağlanıyor. Gelir ve kredi puanı şartı aranmaması da önemli bir avantaj. Ayrıca 6306 sayılı Yasa kapsamındaki uygulamalarda kira yardımı gibi mekanizmalar var. Fakat burada yalnızca desteğin miktarına değil, yurttaşların gerçekte üstlenmek zorunda kaldığı toplam maliyete bakmamız gerekiyor.”

Özellikle düşük ve orta gelir grubundaki yurttaşlar açısından yeni yapı maliyetinin destek tutarını aşan bölümünün ciddi bir finansman yük yaratabileceğini söyleyen Gürbüz, “Sonuçta bir tarafta deprem riski nedeniyle dönüşmek zorunda olan bir yapı var, diğer tarafta bu dönüşümün maliyetini karşılamak zorunda olan bir hane var. Yurttaşların gelirini, borçluluk durumunu ve geçici barınma maliyetini dikkate almayan bir model kağıt üzerinde destekli görünse de uygulamada bazı kesimleri dönüşümün dışında bırakabilir. 6 Şubat depremleri sonrasında da gördüğümüz üzere afetlerin sosyal ve ekonomik etkileri yalnızca yapıların yıkılmasıyla sınırlı kalmıyor; insanların barınma, gelir ve gündelik yaşam düzenleri de ciddi biçimde etkileniyor” diye görüşlerine devam etti.

“Depreme dayanıklı konut bir piyasa malı olmaktan çıkarılıp temel bir kamu politikası hedefi olarak ele alınmalı” ifadelerini kullanan Gürbüz, desteklerin gelir düzeyine, mülkiyet durumuna ve bölgesel maliyetlere göre daha kapsayıcı hale getirilmesi gerektiğini söyledi.

Projelerin denetimini konusunda değerlendirmelerini paylaşan Gürbüz, “Burada iki farklı denetim alanını birbirinden ayırmak gerekiyor. Birincisi, yapının teknik olarak mevzuata ve deprem yönetmeliğine uygun inşa edilip edilmediğini denetleyen yapı denetim sistemi; ikincisi ise dönüşümün planlama, ruhsat, mülkiyet, imar ve kamu yararı boyutunu denetleyen idari süreçler” dedi.

“Ancak bizim açımızdan tartışılması gereken nokta, denetimin yalnızca binanın teknik açıdan doğru yapılmasıyla sınırlı kalmaması. Bir kentsel dönüşüm …

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Naujaat fire damages materials for 8-unit housing project
content:
A fire in Naujaat destroyed one-third of the construction materials intended for an eight-unit public housing project Wednesday night.


A resident watches as plumes of black smoke rise from a fire at an NCC Development construction site in Naujaat on Wednesday. (Photo by Clifford Kringuk)


The fire started around 7:45 p.m. Wednesday at the construction site, the community’s senior administrative officer Chantal Pelletier said in an interview Friday. 


Five firefighters responded to the blaze, using three water trucks and two loaders. The fire was extinguished in about an hour and a half, with crews having to move materials to reach the base of the fire, Pelletier said.


Firefighters then monitored the site for about 12 hours.

No one was injured, she added.


Nunavut Housing Corp. said Thursday it is aware of the fire and confirmed that construction materials for the public housing project were damaged.


“NHC officials are working with the project contractor and local authorities to fully assess the extent of the damage,” the corporation’s communications department said in an emailed statement sent by Winter Fedyk.


NHC said it is waiting for the fire chief’s official report. Once the site can be safely accessed, housing corporation staff and the contractor will conduct a detailed assessment of the damage.


The project was originally scheduled to be completed in June 2027. NHC said it is too early to determine whether the fire will affect that timeline.


“Despite these challenges, NHC will work closely with the contractor to identify steps to keep the project moving forward,” the corporation’s statement said. 


The project is being built by NCC Development, the main contractor for the territorial government’s Nunavut 3000 housing initiative, which aims to build 3,000 new housing units across the territory between 2022 and 2030.


NCC president Juanie Pudluk said in an email that he did not have a comment at this time.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Housing Secretary Took £20k Speaking Fee From Estate Agent Lobbyists
content:
Housing secretary Angela Rayner has taken a £20,000 speaking fee from an estate agents’ lobbying group, even though she once condemned MPs earning money from outside jobs as “beyond shameful”.


Rayner received the fee as part of a two-hour speaking engagement on 12 June at the annual conference of

Propertymark, an industry body

 with over 19,000 members. 


The next month she returned to her ministerial role, having stepped down in 2025 over her failure to pay enough tax on a newly purchased flat.


Rayner spoke at the conference’s “flagship event” in her capacity as the “chief architect” of the Renters’ Right Act, which came into force in England on 1 May.


The event, which included a

Q&A

, was billed as an opportunity for property professionals to hear her speak and grill her over the housing reforms. The payment was made just weeks before Rayner ruled out introducing rent controls in England. There is no suggestion she breached any rules. 


She

told the BBC

 on 24 July that she did not think “rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment”, despite the fact prime minister Andy Burnham

previously backed rent

 freezes as mayor of Greater Manchester.


Propertymark

opposes rent controls

 and lobbied against proposals for a rent freeze.


Rayner’s spokesperson told Novara Media that

“

all earnings have been declared in line with the rules”.


The payment has raised fresh questions over whether ministers should receive money from organisations with interests associated with their ministerial portfolio.


Rayner previously expressed her opposition to rent controls in October 2024. “Rent controls restrict housing supply, which does not help anyone,” she said during a debate on the

Renters’ Rights Bill

.


Between January and June 2026 – during her ten months away from government – Rayner

received roughly £400,000

 in payments and donations from businesses and private individuals, including a £61,500 advance from publisher Bodley Head for a book about her life and political career.


The scale of the earnings is notable given Rayner’s previous attacks on MPs who supplement their parliamentary salaries with outside work.


In March 2023, Rayner commented on an investigation by the pressure group Led By Donkeys, titled MPs for Hire. “This is beyond shameful,” she

wrote on social media

. “Being an MP isn’t a second job. It is the job.”


Nathan Emerson,

chief executive of Propertymark, said:

“Ms Rayner was not serving as a government minister” at the time she was invited to speak at the conference. “There was no indication or expectation that she would subsequently return to government, nor was there any certainty at that point about the future political leadership under Andy Burnham.”


The parliamentary standards committee is looking into whether there should be changes to the rules governing MPs and their outside interests. When approached for comment on Rayner’s case by Novara Media, it said: “

The committee does not comment on individual member activity.”


Susan Hawley, executive director of the charity Spotlight on Corruption, told Novara Media: “

When MPs appear to cash in on their public status for personal gain it is deeply damaging to trust in politicians and in Westminster.


“

This is more than about one individual, however. It is about a system that allows members of parliament to line their pockets outside of their day job without any limits – a system that Rayner rightly criticised and which the Labour government committed to end. Two years on from being elected, however, there is still no sign of the urgent action promised to bring in much stricter controls on MPs’ second jobs. 


“There is no doubt that there will also need to be careful consideration of any conflicts of interest that have arisen from these activities now that Rayner has become a minister again.”

author: Julia Conley
title: Trump Has Dismantled Federal Civil Rights Enforcement, New Report Shows
content:
The White House has decimated staffing at civil rights offices and redirected enforcement toward ideological causes.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Eighteen months into President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House, the administration has systematically gutted the infrastructure within the federal government that for decades had worked to ensure that civil rights and anti-discrimination laws were being enforced—and has turned agencies “against the communities they were meant to protect,” as one researcher at Human Rights Watch said Thursday.

In a new report, the organization detailed how four key agencies have been substantially weakened since Trump took office and almost immediately, with the help of tech billionaire Elon Musk and the Department of Government Efficiency, set about slashing the federal workforce and demanding that the civil servants who remained be “fully on board” with the president’s right-wing agenda.

The report, titled “Remedies Abandoned: US Civil Rights Enforcement Under the Trump Administration,” explains how the US Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Civil Rights Division lost about 75% of its attorneys after the White House told staff that they were not to operate independently from the president; the Office of Civil Rights (OCR) at the Department of Education closed more than half of its regional offices and laid off nearly half its staff in one day; the Fair Housing Office at the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) shrank from 31 staffers to 11; and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission reached its lowest staffing level in over four decades.

With the federal civil rights enforcement workforce decimated, the White House has abandoned discrimination complaints at the four agencies and has carried out demands outlined in Project 2025, the right-wing policy blueprint put forward by the Heritage Foundation. In addition to pushing for the administration to reclassify civil servants like those who were pushed out of their civil rights enforcement roles, the document called for presidential control of the Justice Department and an end to “disparate impact enforcement.”

In April 2025, three months after taking office, Trump signed an executive order directing all federal agencies to eliminate their analysis of disparate impact—the framework that confronts discriminatory policies based on their impacts rather than their intent—to the “maximum degree possible.”

Disparate impact analysis, said HRW, “allows people to challenge hiring criteria, lending practices, school discipline policies, and housing regulations that produce discriminatory outcomes even when no one can identify a smoking gun like a policy that explicitly says ‘exclude Black applicants.’”

The executive order and related directives that followed had a sweeping impact, with HUD dropping seven major housing discrimination and environmental justice cases months later, after they had been ongoing for years.

For example, the agency informed Chicago officials it would no longer monitor the civil rights agreement that had required zoning reform to end concentrated industrial pollution in Black and Latino neighborhoods.

“Department leadership said it would no longer treat environmental harms as fair housing violations in situations without explicit indication of intentional discrimination, in line with President Trump’s April 2025 order seeking to end disparate impact enforcement,” reads the HRW report.

HUD has closed at least 115 fair housing complaints without issuing findings on the claims of discrimination, and career attorneys at the agency filed a whistleblower complaint last September showing they’d been barred from contacting complainants and working with the DOJ to resolve the matters.

“One of the ways we know that our democracy is functioning and healthy is that your rights don’t just disappear because the political winds shift,” said Trey Walk, a US program researcher at HRW.

author: anred
title: Jujuy: viviendo en la intemperie tras la represión y el desalojo a las familias de la Comunidad Santa Rosa en Humahuaca
content:
El operativo policial con maquinaria municipal que el pasado martes dejó a decenas de familias sin vivienda y ha a siete personas detenidas, hoy todavía no tiene respuestas. La Comunidad Santa Rosa debió padecer la represión con balas de goma y gases lacrimógenos en presencia de niños y adultos mayores. La Justicia ejecutó el desalojo sin reconocer que desde la propia Dirección de Catastro habían informado un error en la delimitación de los planos. De esta manera, el operativo avanzó sobre territorio comunitario con el aval del poder político provincial. En estos momentos las familias permanecen a la intemperie asediados por la presencia policial.

Por Johana Arce para ANRed.


Las familias desalojadas permanecen actualmente

a la intemperie y sin un lugar donde vivir

, luego de que las topadoras destruyeran sus viviendas el pasado 11 de agosto. Ante la falta de respuestas, levantaron precarias carpas y ranchos y buscan refugio entre familiares y vecinos, mientras intentan resolver especialmente la situación de niños, niñas y adultos mayores.


La comunidad continúa en permanencia para recuperar el territorio y en estado de alerta frente a nuevos episodios de hostigamiento. La diputada por el Frente de Izquierda (FITU), Natalia Morales en dialogo con ANRed realato la situación complicada de las familias y el maltrato sufrido, «las familias están tratando de proteger a los niños del clima . Estan ayudando vecinos». La legisladora había denunciado el accionar contra la comunidad y las falsas promesas del municipio sobre la posibilidad de otorgar viviendas.


Es así que la situación contrasta con las versiones difundidas por diputados del oficialismo, quienes aseguraron que a las familias se les habían ofrecido viviendas y distintas alternativas habitacionales. Desde la comunidad desmintieron esas afirmaciones y expresaron su indignación:

“Estamos acá a la intemperie, destruyeron todo y están diciendo todo eso”

, señalaron. Hasta el momento, según denunciaron desde la comunidad,

no existe un ofrecimiento concreto por parte de los diputados oficialistas que permita resolver la situación de las familias desalojadas.


El operativo


La orden de desalojo estaba dispuesta para las 10 de la mañana. Durante toda una jornada de violencia, llanto e indignación se desató la represión en el territorio de la Comunidad Indígena Santa Rosa. La Policía, junto al juez, les dio media hora para retirarse y borrar toda una historia generacional, desalojando incluso a mujeres con niños en brazos.


La medida se ejecutó a partir del plano N.º 0809, que fue impugnado por la propia Dirección de Catastro, omitiendo el derecho a la Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada y en un contexto atravesado por denuncias de favores políticos y antecedentes de hostigamiento.


La familia Soruco sostiene que tanto el municipio como distintas áreas del Estado provincial buscan encubrir que los planos estatales se superponen ilegalmente sobre territorio comunitario en el marco de lo que denuncian como “favores políticos”.


“La verdad que la única explicación que encontramos es que es todo político, porque el abogado de la otra parte es funcionario de la Municipalidad de Jujuy”, sostuvo Yoly, presidenta y comunera desalojada.


El conflicto comenzó en 2009, a partir de la aprobación del plano N.º 0809 por parte de la Dirección de Inmuebles de la Provincia de Jujuy, con un trazado gestionado por Nélida Melitona Zerpa Ciares de Chauqui junto a su nieto, Mauricio Ciares Chauqui, miembros de la comunidad, sobre un sector que invade los límites históricos del territorio comunitario.


“Es una familia que está dentro del territorio comunitario. Eso es algo que no pueden hacer porque somos una comunidad y tenemos el artículo 75, inciso 17, donde nos reconoce como comunidades aborígenes”, afirmó.


Pese a que la propia Dirección de Catastro reconoció la equivocación en la delimitación, el plano no fue anulado por la Dirección de Inmuebles y el juez de Primera Instancia en lo Civil y Comercial Juan Pablo Calderón ordenó el desalojo sin constatar el lugar físico que había sido aprobado.

author: Act for freedom now!
title: Those Responsible for the Crisis Have Names and Addresses (Canada)
content:
Why do we break windows? Why did we break your windows (and paint your offices)? Just like every July 1st, many renting households will find themselves on the street. Others will end up in inadequate, substandard, and/or unaffordable housing. In the coming days, we’ll be hearing about the housing crisis. Rising prices. A shortage of available housing. And just like every year, most people will move on to the next story.

We’ve heard it all before. But one thing that’s never discussed—or only mentioned in passing—is who’s responsible for the crisis. The housing crisis didn’t just happen out of thin air. People who find themselves on the streets are not victims of the invisible market. Gentrification and the financialization of housing are not natural phenomena. There are people behind this crisis, people behind this market, people behind these phenomena. And these people have names and addresses. Among those responsible are companies like Iacobo Capital and Denstays. Why these two? Because they have the misfortune (and our good fortune) of being neighbors! The first is a rental and investment company that acquires and manages “undervalued” apartment complexes and units for its investors. Yet this company, which boasts of being a real estate leader, is nothing less than a serial renovictor and a horrible slumlord that plays with the health of its tenants. For its part, Denstays is a short-term rental company with several luxury units in the Plateau, Little Italy, and Mile End. Its executives also rent out properties on Airbnb. The impact of short-term rentals on housing and our communities is well known. Denstays is actively contributing to this trend.

Anyway, on the night of June 30 to July 1, we decided to take matters into our own hands. Why did we smash your windows (and paint your offices)? Because we’re sick of seeing so much energy and resources wasted on lobbying elected officials for unfortunately often paltry gains and on organizing peaceful protests for the right to housing. Instead, we decided to smash your windows. To physically attack your workspaces (just so you know, we’re not heartless—we don’t attack your living spaces, unlike you). To make you pay the price of your responsibility. An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Or something like that.

Now we hope that other nighttime troublemakers will feel inspired to take matters into their own hands ;p

title: Ο Αύγουστος της Αλληλεγγύης: Τριήμερο Camp στα Προσφυγικά 14, 15, 16 Αυγούστου
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Ο Αύγουστος της Αλληλεγγύης: Τριήμερο Camp στα Προσφυγικά 14, 15, 16 Αυγούστου


English below


Σας καλούμε όλες/όλους/όλα σε ένα ολοήμερο – τριήμερο camp στην Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, από την Παρασκευή 14/8 στις 18:00 ως την Κυριακή 16/8. Ένα τριήμερο γεμάτο με εκδηλώσεις, παιχνίδια, δραστηριότητες και μουσική. Με καθημερινές συλλογικές κουζίνες, χρόνο και χώρο για συζητήσεις και ανατροφοδότηση, συλλογικές δράσεις και κατασκήνωση στους χώρους της Κοινότητας.


Τους τελευταίους 6 μήνες, κορυφώθηκε και συνεχίζει να εξελίσσεται ένας μεγάλος αγώνας ζωής και θανάτου για την υπεράσπιση των Προσφυγικών, ενάντια στην εκκένωση, τον εκτοπισμό και τη διάλυση του μεγαλύτερου αυτοοργανωμένου εγχειρήματος κοινωνικής στέγασης, αλληλεγγύης και κοινής ωφέλειας στην Ελλάδα. Απέναντι στα Προσφυγικά και σε όλο τον κόσμο της αλληλεγγύης βρίσκεται ένα κοινωνιοκτόνο καθεστώς και ο περιφερειάρχης Ν. Χαρδαλιάς, τα σχέδια εξευγενισμού και η πολιτική της καταστολής των κινημάτων και των ανθρώπων που παλεύουν για τη ζωή και την αξιοπρέπεια.


Οι 400 κάτοικοι από διαφορετικές γεωγραφίες, κουλτούρες, θρησκείες και ιδεολογίες είναι το μωσαϊκό όπου εδώ και 16 χρόνια συναρτά την Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών. Και είναι αυτό το μωσαϊκό που εδώ και 16 χρόνια λειτουργεί ως ένα ζωντανό παράδειγμα στο εδώ και στο τώρα, για το πώς τόσο διαφορετικοί μεταξύ τους άνθρωποι δημιουργούν καθημερινά σχέσεις ισότητας, αλληλεγγύης και αλληλοβοήθειας και συγκροτούν μια κοινότητα αγώνα, αυτοοργάνωσης και συμπερίληψης.


Μοιραστήκαμε έναν αγώνα δίκαιο, ανιδιοτελή και συλλογικό, όχι μόνο για τους κατοίκους των Προσφυγικών, αλλά για κάθε άνθρωπο που ενεπλάκησε σε αυτόν από όποιο μετερίζι, αλλά και για ολόκληρη την κοινωνία. Για το δικαίωμα στη στέγη, τη ζωή, την αξιοπρέπεια, το δικαίωμα των ανθρώπων να οργανώνονται, να αυτοοργανώνονται, να ορίζουν τις ζωές τους σε σκοτεινούς καιρούς.


Μέσα σε αυτούς τους καιρούς, λοιπόν, η απειλή εκκένωσης την περίοδο του Αύγουστου επανέρχεται για κάθε απελευθερωμένο χώρο, με τον συγκεκριμένο Αύγουστο να βρίσκει το έδαφος των Προσφυγικών στο επίκεντρο του κρατικού σχεδιασμού, όπως επανειλημμένα έχει δηλώσει δημοσίως ο κυβερνητικός εκπρόσωπος Π.Μαρινάκης.


Σήμερα, σχεδόν έξι μήνες μετά από την έναρξη αυτού του όμορφου αγώνα και έχοντας ήδη κατακτήσει την πρώτη μεγάλη νίκη, σηκώνοντας συλλογικά την ευθύνη και το κόστος με τον σύντροφό μας Αριστοτέλη Χαντζή ακόμη να διατρέχει άμεσο κίνδυνο για τη ζωή και την υγεία του στη ΜΕΘ του Ευαγγελισμού, συνεχίζουμε να κρατάμε ψηλά τη σημαία του αγώνα και παραμένουμε στο έδαφός μας, πιο ενδυναμωμένοι/ες/α από ποτέ.


Σας περιμένουμε όλους/ολες/όλα σε αυτό το τριήμερο camp στα Προσφυγικά για να γιορτάσουμε την αλληλεγγύη, να αναστοχαστούμε και να μοιραστούμε την καθημερινότητα με ολοήμερη διαμονή και συλλογικές δράσεις στο φυσικό έδαφος που δόθηκε αυτός ο αγώνας.

author: Free Mumia Berlin
title: Abschaffung der Todesstrafe überall! Stoppen wir die Hinrichting von Keith LaMar!
content:
Kommt am 10. Oktober 2026, dem internationalen Tag gegen die Todesstrafe, von 19 – 20:00 Uhr vor die US Botschaft, Pariser Pl. 2 – U5-Brandenburger Tor


Noch immer wird die Todesstrafe, also das staatliche Ermorden von Gefangenen in vielen Teilen der Welt durchgeführt. Seit vielen Jahren lässt sich zwar ein weltweiter Trend gegen die Todesstrafe beobachten, aber es ist genau wie mit allen anderen Kämpfen für Gerechtigkeit und um Befreiung: neben den Erfolgen gibt es auch Stillstand und Rückschläge. Neben China mit den meisten Hinrichtungen der Welt sehen wir das auch in drei Ländern, die in letzter Zeit immer wieder im Zentrum der internationalen Aufmerksamkeit stehen, nämlich im Iran (zur brutalen Niederschlagung von Massenprotesten) , Israel (mit rassistischer Sondergesetzgebung) und den USA (zur Erhaltung der Weißen Vorherrschaft). Kein Staat hat das Recht, Gefangene zu foltern und zu töten!


Ein Gefangener im US Bundesstaat Ohio kämpft derzeit gegen seine drohende Hinrichtung und den Rassismus und Klassismus, die seinem Urteil zu Grunde liegen: Keith LaMar. Er wurde nach dem Lucasville Gefängnisaufstand von 1993 zum Tode verurteilt. Er wurde für den Tod mehrerer Schließer verantwortlich gemacht. Dabei ist unstrittig, dass er gar nicht an dem Aufstand teilgenommen hat. Der Afroamerikaner Keith LaMar wurde von einer ausschließlich weißen Jury für schuldig befunden. Er hatte zuvor sich und andere Gefangene als Jailhouse Lawyer (Gefangenenanwalt) juristisch gegen die willkürliche Gewalt im Knast verteidigt und war den Behörden ein Dorn im Auge. Zuerst wurde ihm ein Deal angeboten: er solle sich schuldig bekennen, um die nach dem Aufstand über die Zustände im bundesstaatlichen Gefängnis empörte Öffentlichkeit zu beruhigen und Kritik verstummen zu lassen. Dafür wurde ihm keine Verschärfung seiner ursprünglichen Haft in Aussicht gestellt. LaMar verweigerte das und wurde ohne Chance auf Verteidigung durch gefälschte Aussagen in einer rassistisch aufgeladenen Verhandlung in wenigen Stunden zum Tod verurteilt. Am 13. Januar 2027 will Ohio ihn nun mit der Giftspritze ermorden.

title: Altıncı günde de Bakanlık önündeler: Madenciler hakları için eylemi sürdürüyor
content:
Bağımsız Maden-İş Sendikası üyesi, Yıldızlar SSS Holding’e bağlı Elazığ Eti Gümüş ile Doruk Madencilik işçilerinin haklarını alma talebiyle 10 Ağustos’ta başlattığı eylem sürüyor.


İşçiler eylemlerinin altıncı gününde, gözaltından serbest bırakıldıktan sonra Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı önünde bir araya geldi. Oturma eylemine devam etti.


ANKA'nın aktardığına göre baretlerini yere vuran içiler, "Bakanlık halka hesap verecek", "Holdinglere el pençe, madenciye işkence", "Alparslan Bayraktar peşimizi bırak" ve "Hak, hukuk, adalet" sloganları attı.


Öte yandan işçiler, Bağımsız Maden İş Sendikası Örgütlenme Uzmanı Başaran Aksu'nun gözaltında olmasına tepki göstererek, "Başaran Aksu serbest kalsın" diye de slogan attı. 


Burada konuşan Bağımsız Maden-İş Sendikası Genel Başkanı Gökay Çakır, 10 Ağustos’tan bugüne 4 kez gözaltına alındıklarını hatırlattı. Ayrıca sendikanın Örgütlenme Uzmanı Başaran Aksu’nun "halkı kin ve düşmanlığa tahrik" suçlamasıyla halen gözaltında tutulduğunu söyledi.


"Burada keyfimizden durmuyoruz"


Şöyle konuştu:


"Bizler buraya gözaltına alınmaya gelmedik. Başaran Aksu mahkemeye çıkacak, hiçbir suçu yokken. İnsanlar eleştirilebilir ama ne yazık ki bizim ülkemizde eleştiri yaptığınız zaman gözaltına alınıyorsunuz ya da tutuklanıyorsunuz. İnsanları susturmaya, insanları daha çok ezmeye yönelik holdingler, siyasetçiler buna göre gard alıyorlar.Bizler de işçiler olarak, en azından işçi sınıfı olarak, ikişer cümle bile söylesek bizim için onurdur, gururdur. Başaran abimizi gözaltına alabilirler, içeri de atabilirler. Bizler buradayız. Bizleri de gözaltına alabilirler ama bu mücadeleyi bizden sonra gelecek arkadaşlarımız da devam ettirecek.


Beni de tutuklayabilirler ama bu, işçi sınıfına yakışmayan hareketler oluyor. Holdinglerin baskısıyla birilerini tutuklamayı kar yapıyoruz sanıyorlar. Kar yapmaz, siz daha çok zarar edersiniz. Evet, paralar ödendi bir kısmı paralar ödendi. İşçinin çoğu alacağı, yüzde 90'ı duruyor daha. Ondan sonra da bütün medyalarda ‘paralar ödenmiş, siz orada niye duruyorsunuz?’ Biz orada babamızın hayrına, keyfimizden durmuyoruz. Biz de gözaltına alınmayı çok istemiyoruz. Bizim de ailemiz var, bizim de çocuklarımız var. Biz de bir an önce evimize gitmek istiyoruz. Bu işçilerin hakkı ne zaman ödenirse, o zamana kadar da gitmeyeceğiz."


"O lafları söyletmemek için işçinin hakkını ödeyeceksiniz"


Çakır ayrıca "Başaran Aksu’ya mı bağlı bu ülkedeki kin? Başaran Aksu’ya mı bağlı bu ülkedeki öfke? Burası Türkiye Cumhuriyeti ise insanlar cümleler söyleyebilir. Kimsenin bundan gocunmaması lazım. O lafları söyletmemek için işçinin hakkını ödeyeceksiniz. Mahkemeye çıkacak. Başaran abinin bugün serbest kalacağına inanıyorum" diye konuştu.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: TalkTV Presenter Found Guilty of Assaulting Climate Protester
content:
Rightwing news presenter Andr

é

 Walker has been found guilty of assault after attempting to kick, punch and strangle a climate protester at a pro-Trump gala dinner in Windsor last year.


The Republican Overseas event, held at Windsor Guildhall in September, was ambushed by Fossil Free London protesters Robin Wells and Kush Naker. The pair protested US president Donald Trump’s climate policies by chanting: “If you drill, baby, drill, how many will you kill?” and unfurling a banner.


Video footage showed Walker, the event’s organiser and a host on TalkTV, dragging Naker from the dinner and into another room. In a YouTube video recorded after the incident, Walker mentioned the side room had no CCTV, grinned and raised his thumbs at the camera. 


A court has now upheld that Walker attempted to assault Naker once he was not being filmed. The YouTuber received an 18-month conditional discharge and must pay a £1,200 fine, including £550 compensation to his victim.


Walker slammed his palm on the desk and swore when he heard the guilty verdict at Reading Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, the Byline Times reported.


Naker, an NHS doctor, said: “Using violence to silence free speech is a hallmark of fascism.

André

 Walker’s response to hearing us criticise deadly fossil fuel addiction gave us a glimpse of what happens when extreme rightwing populist narratives build their movements on hate.”


Wells added: “This verdict sends an important message that being a protester does not mean surrendering your right to be treated with dignity and respect.” 


“Fossil Free London will continue to stand up to politicians, corporations and powerful interests whose decisions are putting billions of lives at risk. We will never be intimidated into silence.”

title: Miners’ protest enters its fifth day
content:
Miners who are members of the Independent Mine Workers’ Union and employed by Elazığ Eti Gümüş and Doruk Madencilik, both affiliated with Yıldızlar SSS Holding, continued their protest in Ankara, demanding payment of their unpaid wages and compensation. Gathering outside the Ministry of Energy, on Thursday, the miners removed their work clothes and chanted slogans including “We will win through resistance” and “Victory will belong to the resisting miners.”


Independent Mine Workers’ Union President Gökay Çakır said, “We want to meet with the ministry. It was the ministry that promised us payment. Let the ministry resolve this issue. We will not leave here until our demands are met.”


Workers from Doruk Madencilik said they would continue their protest with determination.


The miners are continuing their protest outside the ministry, banging their helmets on the ground.

title: Criminalización de la protesta: la campaña por la libertad para Milton y Eneas vuelve a las calles
content:
Eneas Gallo y Milton Tolomeo. Imagen: Archivo.


La campaña por la libertad de Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo vuelve a las calles con dos nuevas convocatorias. Este sábado 15 de agosto desde las 18.30 se realizará un festival solidario en «Oxido y Resistencia» (Avenida Don Pedro de Mendoza 1667, CABA) y el próximo miércoles 19 a las 16 habrá una movilización al Congreso Nacional – que confluirá con la habitual marcha de jubilados/as – para exigir la libertad inmediata de ambos trabajadores, detenidos con prisión preventiva tras participar de las protestas contra la reforma laboral impulsada por el gobierno de Javier Milei.

Las nuevas acciones son parte de una campaña que viene sumando organizaciones sociales, políticas, sindicales, estudiantiles y de derechos humanos y que, tras un plenario realizado en julio, resolvió profundizar las iniciativas de difusión, solidaridad y movilización para denunciar la criminalización de la protesta.

Por ANRed.


La

campaña por la libertad de Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo

 vuelve a las calles durante agosto con nuevas actividades para

exigir la liberación de los dos trabajadores detenidos en el marco de las movilizaciones contra la reforma laboral del gobierno de Javier Milei

.


Este

sábado 15 de agosto desde las 18.30 se realizará un festival solidario en «Oxido y Resistencia» (Avenida Don Pedro de Mendoza 1667, CABA).


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Coordinadora por la libertad de lxs presxs políticxs (@coordi.presxspoliticxs)


Mientras que el

próximo miércoles 19 desde las 16 se realizará una movilización al Congreso Nacional convocada por la

Coordinadora por la Libertad de lxs Presxs Políticxs

, la que confluirá con la habitual movilización de jubilados/as.


Con estas dos convocatorias, desde la campaña buscan ampliar su alcance. El pasado 18 de julio, casi un centenar de activistas y representantes de unas treinta organizaciones participaron de un plenario en el Espacio de Memoria ex CCD “El Infierno”, en Avellaneda. Allí se discutieron estrategias para fortalecer la campaña y se resolvió impulsar una campaña audiovisual, una recolección masiva de firmas y una movilización para el 19 de agosto.


El encuentro también permitió incorporar nuevos espacios al funcionamiento de la Coordinadora y reafirmar la necesidad de vincular la defensa de Milton y Eneas con las distintas luchas sociales que atraviesan el país.

Desde la campaña sostienen que la libertad de ambos trabajadores constituye una demanda que excede sus situaciones particulares y se relaciona directamente con la defensa del derecho a protestar y organizarse

.


Foto: Sofía Saluzzi.


Las nuevas convocatorias llegan, además, después de

varios meses de prisión preventiva y en un contexto en el que distintas organizaciones vienen denunciando un avance de la judicialización de las manifestaciones, el ciberpatrullaje, las detenciones y el uso de herramientas penales contra quienes participan de protestas

. En este contexto, para la campaña, el caso de Milton y Eneas se convirtió así en una bandera contra la criminalización de la protesta social.


Milton Tolomeo y Eneas Gallo permanecen detenidos con prisión preventiva en el penal de Marcos Paz luego de haber participado de las protestas contra la reforma laboral. Tolomeo fue detenido el 15 de febrero y Gallo el 18 de marzo. Gallo es trabajador precarizado de la aplicación Pedidos Ya e integrante de una asamblea de General Rodríguez, mientras que Tolomeo es trabajador precarizado y participa de una asamblea barrial de Lanús.


La situación de ambos viene siendo denunciada por organizaciones sociales, políticas, sindicales y de derechos humanos como un caso de criminalización de la protesta. En mayo, la Legislatura porteña aprobó un proyecto de declaración que expresó su “más enérgico repudio” a las detenciones y reclamó su inmediata libertad, además de advertir sobre las condiciones de encierro y las restricciones que atraviesan ambos detenidos. En el caso de Tolomeo, organizaciones de derechos humanos denunciaron especialmente su traslado inicial a un sector destinado a personas consideradas de “alto riesgo” en el penal de Ezeiza.


En tanto, la

Comisión Provincial por la Memoria

 también viene señalando la

sistematicidad de la represión y la criminalización de la protesta desde la aplicación del denominado «protocolo antipiquetes».

title: „Tag der Ehre“ und „Lukov-Marsch“ 2023: Deutsche Polizei behindert Antifa-Proteste in Bulgarien und verfolgt Angriffe auf Nazis in Ungarn
content:
Dossier


„Am 24. Februar 2023 wurde Florian Gutsche, Bundesvorsitzender der VVN-BdA, am Berliner Flughafen von Beamten der Bundespolizei im Rahmen einer offensichtlich vorbereiteten Aktion abgefangen. Gutsche war auf dem Weg nach Bulgarien, wo er als Beobachter an internationalen Protesten gegen den faschistischen „Lukov-Marsch“ in Sofia teilnehmen wollte. Er wurde zwei Stunden festgehalten und befragt, sein Gepäck durchsucht und mit einer sechsseitigen „Ausreiseuntersagung“ wieder entlassen. Diese beinhaltete die Drohung, dass man ihn bei Zuwiderhandlung „in Gewahrsam nehmen“ und strafrechtlich verfolgen werde. Das Ausreiseverbot wurde im Rahmen des Passgesetzes für jegliche Auslandsreise an dem Wochenende erlassen. Die Verfügung wurde damit begründet, dass damit zu rechnen sei, dass Gutsche „das Ansehen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland im Ausland erheblich schädigen“ würde…“

Pressemitteilung der VVN-BdA vom 6. März 2023


 und mehr daraus sowie dazu:


Gewaltsamer Übergriff durch 5 männliche Vollzugsbeamte im Gefängnis in Budapest: Maja T. in Ungarn wegen Tragens eines Kleides misshandelt


„

Ein fünfköpfiges Kommando soll Maja T. gewaltsam ausgezogen haben, da »Frauenkleidung« im Männerknast verboten sei. Weitere Konsequenzen drohen.


Eine Unterstützungsgruppe berichtete am Dienstag von einem gewaltsamen Übergriff auf Maja T. im Gefängnis in Budapest. Ausschließlich männliche Vollzugsbeamte hätten die non-binäre Antifaschist*in am 17. Juli in der Zelle zu Boden geworfen, festgehalten und ihr Handschellen angelegt. T. habe dabei eine geplatzte Lippe, eine Quetschung am Ohr sowie Schmerzen am Kiefer und an der Schläfe erlitten. Vorausgegangen war laut dem »Solidaritätskomitee für Maja« ein mündliches Verbot des Sicherheitschefs, als »Frauenkleidung« gelesene Kleider oder Röcke zu tragen – diese seien »in einem Männerknast verboten«. T. hatte sich aber geweigert, ein Kleid auszuziehen. (…)


Die Beamten hätten laut dem Solidaritätskomitee auch gewaltsam versucht, das Tragen des Kleids zu unterbinden. T. sei unter Schmerzgriffen in ein ärztliches Behandlungszimmer gebracht und zwangsweise entkleidet worden. Das Kleid sei weggenommen und durch ein Polo-Shirt ersetzt worden. Sämtliche als »Frauenkleidung« gelesene Stücke seien aus der Zelle entfernt und eingelagert worden. Beim Abtransport ins Krankenhaus sei Maja T. mit Handschellen, Gürtel und Fußfesseln gesichert und von einem sechsköpfigen, mit Maschinengewehren bewaffneten Kommando begleitet worden. Auch Jarosch bestätigt das. Gegen T. wurde danach ein Disziplinarverfahren eingeleitet, mit der Begründung, die Beamten angegriffen zu haben. Das Solidaritätskomitee und Vater Jarosch weisen diese Darstellung zurück. (…)


Jarosch verwies zudem auf die Rechtsprechung des Bundesverfassungsgerichts, das dem Berliner Kammergericht vorgehalten hatte, sich bei der als rechtswidrig beurteilten Auslieferungsentscheidung vor zwei Jahren auf pauschale Zusicherungen Ungarns zur Behandlung von LGBTIQ+-Personen in Haft verlassen zu haben. Die bloße Erklärung, man werde sich an die Europäischen Strafvollzugsgrundsätze des Europarats und die Nelson-Mandela-Regeln halten, reiche nicht aus, so das Gericht. (…)


»Jeder Mensch soll das Recht haben, seine Geschlechtsidentität auszuleben«, fordert Wolfram Jarosch. Sollte sich zudem bestätigen, dass Maja T. anlässlich der Misshandlungen der Kontakt zu ihrem ungarischen Anwalt verwehrt worden ist, sei das ein weiterer Skandal. Sowohl die ungarische als auch die deutsche Regierung müssten zu den Haftbedingungen in Budapest eingreifen, so Jarosch

…“

author: Jules Arpula
title: Media hysteria shows high schoolers are right to protest Pauline Hanson
content:
There’s one thing I’ve learned organising the nationwide student walkout against Pauline Hanson, and it’s something they don’t tell you at school: If you’re a student protester, you cop more criticism from the establishment than if you’re a far-right politician who supports mass deportations and abortion bans.

Since we announced that we’re walking out of school on Thursday, there’s been a flood of hit pieces in the right-wing press, furious debates on talkback radio, and denunciations from politicians. The response just confirms why it’s so important for us to stand up—because the capitalist media and politicians aren’t going to. They’re up to their necks in complicity with Hanson’s rise, and they want to demonise anyone who has the guts to call her out.

The arguments against our strike are mind-bogglingly stupid. It’s funny to be lectured about staying in school by some of the dumbest people in Australia.

Liberal Party nepo-baby and 3AW shock-jock Tom Elliot, who graciously had me on his show, mused to his listeners: “Why underage students, who can’t even vote, are so worried about Pauline Hanson, I just don’t know”.

That’s a head-scratcher. We don’t enjoy even the very limited democratic rights afforded to adults, but we’re already seeing the way the rise of the far right is going to change our lives for the worse. We’ve been watching Trump’s rampage in the United States, as he’s slashed social services, threatened entire nations with annihilation and used immigration Gestapo thugs to terrorise and deport residents. We’ve watched as far-right riots have spread across the European continent and throughout Britain. But, according to Tom Elliot, what is there to worry about?

Plenty of journalists have said we need to stay in school and focus on our grades. Lucy Zelic asked in the

Daily Telegraph

, “With NAPLAN results sinking, why are we preaching Hanson hate in class?”

Let me spell it out. Hanson’s not going to put her racist rampage on pause until we all get our university degrees. The Victorian state election is in three months, and One Nation is building a far-right organisation to go out and win seats. She’s shaping politics right here, right now—putting migrant bashing, misogyny and attacks on workers at the centre of the discussion. If this is what we’re seeing already, what will it be like in five years when we’re entering the workforce?

The condescension echoes what we heard throughout the Palestine solidarity movement, when Premier Ben Carroll, who was then the education minister, warned us to leave politics up to our parents, and stay in school if we want to change the world.

These people clearly missed a few history lessons. Students have been central to movements for social change forever—from the high-schoolers who challenged segregation in the US South in the 1950s, to the heroic school kids who were massacred in the Soweto uprising in South Africa, to the role that school students have played across the world in the global Palestine solidarity movement. Those of us who have actually studied this history know you change the world by organising together, not by becoming soulless career politicians like Carroll.

In the

Herald Sun

, Andrew Bolt said that we are being “played” by socialist agitators, “extremists manipulating [us], with violence on their mind”.

High schoolers don’t need to be told what to think about Hanson. It’s pretty obvious that it’s racist to call for monoculture. It’s pretty obvious that it’s sexist to blame women for domestic violence. It’s pretty obvious that she’s backed by a coterie of rich creeps who want to roll back workers’ rights and line their pockets further.

I’m a member of the High School Anticapitalists in Melbourne, who identify Hanson as a hard-edged outgrowth of capitalist politics, in lockstep with the priorities of competition, nationalism and profit.

Although the high school walkout was initiated by High School Anticapitalists, it’s spread far and wide, to places where we have no members. Students from Bendigo to Geraldton to Tasmania are organising their own local walkouts, painting banners, and getting in touch with our group.

But it shouldn’t be surprising that socialists are behind the strike. The only political party that has wholeheartedly backed what we are doing in Melbourne is the Victorian Socialists. I think socialist politics is about standing on the right side of history, not cow-towing to what’s considered “reasonable” and …

title: Kaynarpınar Köyündeki JES projesine karşı Bayraklı'da eylem
content:
İzmir – Bayraklı'da bulunan Karlıova Yedisu Kültür Derneği'nde, Muş'un Varto ilçesi ile Bingöl'ün Karlıova ilçesi arasında kalan Kaynarpınar köyünde planlanan Jeotermal Elektrik Santrali (JES) projesine karşı basın açıklaması yapıldı.

Yamanlar Mahalllesi'nde bulunan dernek binası önünde yapılan açıklamaya çok sayıda dernek üyesi ve kurum temsilcisi katıldı.

Basın açıklamasını okuyan Peri Vadisi İzmir Temsilcisi Nilüfer Uygun, H2 Enerji/İGNİS şirketinin kuracağı jeotermal santrallerin Peri vadisinin, köylerin ve ekosistemin kalbine yerleştirileceğine dikkat çekti.

Santrallerin doğal dengeyi bozacağını, yöre halkının sağlığını olumsuz etkileyeceğini, oluşacak gürültünün yaşamı çekilmez kılacağını, arazi çökmelerinin olabileceğini dile getiren Uygun, "Açılacak poligonlar ve inşa edilecek yapılar halihazırda dar olan arazilerimize sığmayacaktır. Bu durum köylülerimizin evleri dahil tapulu mülklerinin kamulaştırılması, halkın topraksızlaştırılması ve köylerinden göçe zorlanması demektir" dedi.

Proje sahasının, en riskli fay sistemlerinden biri olan Kuzey Anadolu Fay Hattı ile (KAF), Doğu Anadolu Fay Hattı'nın (DAF) kesiştiği, "Karlıova Üçlü Eklemi" üzerinde olduğunu ifade eden Uygun, yer altına uygulanacak yüksek basınçlı enjeksiyonların büyük depremleri tetikleme riski taşıdığını belirtti.

Tüm bu tehlikelere karşı Varto'da başlatılan direnişin bugün itibarıyla 100. gününe girdiğini dile getiren Uygun, bugün Kaynarpınar köyünde yeni bir nöbet çadırı kurulduğu bilgisini paylaştı.

Uygun, buralarda 24 saat nöbet tutulduğunu belirterek, "Şirketin kolluk kuvvetleri eşliğinde cuma ve pazar günleri başlattığı şantiye kurma ve kazı girişimleri, halkımızın kitlesel ve kararlı duruşuyla durdurulmuştur" dedi.

Şirketler ve ortakları bölgeyi tamamen terk edene kadar meşru ve hukuki mücadelelerini büyüterek sürdüreceklerini vurgulayan Uygun, tüm doğa savunucularını, çevre örgütlerini, kamuoyunu Varto ve

Karlıova halkının direnişine destek olmaya çağırdı.

Eylemde, "Kaynarpınar yalnız değildir",

"Sermaye şaşırma sabrımızı taşırma" sloganları atıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Iranian Ministry of Intelligence forces arrest 11 Kurdish citizens in four cities
content:
Iranian Ministry of Intelligence forces have arrested at least 11 Kurdish citizens in Oshnavieh, Bukan, Miandoab and Mahabad in West Azerbaijan Province.


Those arrested are Sedigh Karimi, Masoud Alani Kohneh-Ghaleh, Hadi Azizi, Omid Chavbazi, Amir Soleymani, Mohammad Hajizadeh, Shwana Divazi, Loghman Ghorbani, Rahman Khouzan, Esmaeil Badsar and Zakaria Badsar.


On 13 August, Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested four citizens from Bukan: Shwana Divazi, Loghman Ghorbani, former political prisoner Sedigh Karimi and Hadi Azizi, the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) reported learned.


A day later, the forces raided family homes and arrested Rahman Khouzan, from the village of Gol Marzanik in Bukan; Omid Chavbazi, from Bukan; and Mohammad Hajizadeh, from the village of Gavmish Goli in Miandoab.


On 15 August, Ministry of Intelligence forces raided Zakaria Badsar’s family home in Bukan to arrest him.


When they found that he was not there, they arrested his father, Esmaeil Badsar, and held him hostage. Zakaria Badsar turned himself in at the Intelligence Ministry office in Bukan several hours later, after which his father was released.


On the same day, security forces arrested Amir Soleymani, from the village of Khorkhoreh in Mahabad, at his family home.


Ministry of Intelligence forces also arrested Kurdish singer Masoud Alani Kohneh-Ghaleh, from Oshnavieh, at a café in the city at noon.


Following his arrest, the forces raided his family home and confiscated several personal items belonging to members of his family, including their mobile phones.


Alani Kohneh-Ghaleh has repeatedly been summoned and arrested in recent years over composing Kurdish epic and revolutionary songs.


The forces arrested the 11 Kurdish citizens without warrants and used violence during the arrests.


Despite repeated visits and continued enquiries by their families, the security and judicial authorities have refused to respond or provide any explanation.


No information is yet available regarding the reasons for their arrests or the charges brought against them.

author: anonym
title: Hand in Hand mit CDU und Polizei gegen das La Casa
content:
Am Morgen des 5. Augusts 2026 fand ein geheimes Treffen zwischen dem illegetim übernommenen Vereinsvorstand des Hausprojektes AJZ Kita/ La Casa, der Berliner Polizei und der Bezirksbürgermeisterin von Marzahn-Hellersdorf, Nadja Zivcovic (CDU), statt.


Bei dem geheimen Meeting im Rathaus dürfte es um die Vorbereitung von Repressionsmaßnahmen gegen die Menschen, die das AJZ Kita nutzen, bewohnen und betreiben, gegangen sein. Eine solche offene Zusammenarbeit von selbsternannten linken Strukturen mit rassistischen Parteien und den Cops ist ein neuer Tiefpunkt.


Wir anonymisieren die Namen im Folgenden Text, um sie nicht in der Öffentlichkeit zu outen.


Was zuvor geschah?


Die Geschehnisse am 4. Juli 2026 rund um die gescheiterte „Besetzung“ des AJZ Kita in Marzahn-Hellersdorf durch einen Schlägertrupp sind bereits hinlänglich dargestellt worden (https://kontrapolis.info/18262/ | https://kontrapolis.info/18264/ | https://kontrapolis.info/18273/). Doch zum Hintergrund der Geschehnisse gehört auch die Rolle des Vorstands vom Trägerverein des AJZ Kita. Innerhalb des letzten Jahres wurde der Vereinsvorstand des AJZ Kita im Zuge einer geplanten Aktion von einer kleinen Personengruppe übernommen. Dabei wurden zum Teil Personen eingesetzt, die seit Jahren nicht mehr im Haus oder im Bezirk aktiv waren. Dutzende Personen erschienen plötzlich auf der Vereinsversammlung des Hauses – ohne, dass sich die derzeitigen Hausbewohnenden und Hausnutzenden dagegen wehren konnten. Dadurch gelang es ihnen, eine Mehrheit bei der Wahl zu konstruieren, um teilweise fremde, ältere Männer in den Vorstand zu putschen. Seither wird der Vorstandsposten genutzt, um Hausbewohner*innen und Hausnutzenden mit unliebsamen politischen Positionen repressiv entgegenzutreten oder Einzüge und Nutzungen von neuen Menschen gänzlich zu verhindern.


Hierbei wird eigenmächtig und autoritär, ungeachtet des Willens der langjährig bestehenden Wohngemeinschaften und Nutzer*innen sowie der ursprünglichen Ziele des Vereins, entschieden. Der Vorstand agiert somit nicht im Sinne eines autonomen, antifaschistischen Jugendprojekts, sondern allein nach seinen eigenen politischen Vorstellungen. Dass es für diese Selbstherrlichkeit keine Grenzen mehr gibt, zeigte sich auch beispielhaft am Geheimtreffen am 5. August im Hellersdorfer Rathaus.


Wer sucht den Schulterschluss mit der CDU und den Cops?


Am Morgen des 5. August liefen wir über den Alice-Salomon-Platz und sahen plötzlich einen der Vereinsvorstände des La Casa am Hellersdorfer Rathaus. Weil wir uns fragten, was er dort macht, haben wir die Situation beobachtet. Im Folgenden nennen wir die Person „N. B.“. N. B. war innerhalb des letzten Jahres nach mehreren Jahren erstmals wieder im AJZ Kita/ La Casa. Er tauchte – für viele Hausbewohner*innen als gänzlich Unbekannter – bei der Mitgliederversammlung auf, um sich in den Vorstand wählen zu lassen. N. B. scheint nicht in Marzahn-Hellersdorf wohnhaft zu sein und ist darüber hinaus weder in den Jahren vor der Vorstandswahl noch heute aktiv im Kontext des Hauses AJZ Kita/ La Casa gewesen. Auch langjährige Hausbewohner*innen und Nutzer*innen kennen diese Person nicht. Seine Absichten, der Vorstand eines Projekts zu werden, in dem er weder wohnt noch politisch oder sozial aktiv ist, erscheinen uns mehr als fragwürdig.


Als an die Macht geputschter Vorstand, der das Haus und seine Nutzer*innen kaum noch kennt, scheint er das Objekt nun als seines zu betrachten. Vor der CDU-Bürgermeisterin und den Bullen spielt er sich offensichtlich als alleiniger Repräsentant des Vorstands auf.


Wie es zu dem Treffen im Hellersdorfer Rathaus kam, ist unklar. Der Machtmissbrauch, den sich Einzelpersonen durch Übernahme von bürokratischen Posten sichern, ist für linke Projekte leider nichts Neues, die aktive Zusammenarbeit mit Polizei und Politik gegen die eigenen Leute ist dennoch ein Besorgnis erregendes Maß neuer Eskalation, das sich in eine Kette von Eskalationen zum Erhhalt eigener Autorität einreiht. Nach dem gewaltsamen Angriff der Gruppe „Reclaim La Casa“ auf gegenwärtige Hausbewohnende gibt es in linken Bewegungen Berlins kaum noch Rückhalt für die Unterstützer*innen des selbsternannten Räumkommandos. Stattdessen sucht der ins Amt geputschte Vorstand nun auf anderem Wege nach Möglichkeiten, um sich mit Hilfe von CDU und Polizei an der Macht zu halten. When we speak, it should be clear, to show reality and not to obscure it and/or reduce it to a spectacle.


 We issue a warning about suspicious, manipulative and reckless individual(s) behind the “FAI ARCHIVE” – just set up by the “No War But My War” blog and Instagram, who have been trying to contact admins and sites in the international counter-information networks and anti-repression solidarity groups in a duplicitous way and spreading misinformations and smears. We note that

FAI

/

FRI

[1]

 has been recently designated as a foreign terrorist organisation by the American administration for which they also target “

Antifa Ost

“, etc, as part of a hyped and aggressive move against domestic and foreign radical-left and anti-state anarchist movements and tendencies of all sorts, including single-issue unrelated subjects to anarchism.
