title: TJA activist Saliha Ayata: Women are the leading force for peace
content:
Following the adoption of the “Framework Law” by Parliament, the law is now expected to enter into force. As attention turns to what other steps will be taken, the Tevgera Jinên Azad (TJA) issued a call stressing that women must also be involved in the ongoing process and that women’s monitoring commissions should be established. In its call, TJA also stressed that women must be represented in decision-making mechanisms and drew attention to women’s demands in the process. Speaking about women’s demands and the call, TJA activist Saliha Ayata said, “This is a new beginning for us.”


 


‘Women are at the forefront of the struggle’


Drawing attention to the importance of the process reached, Saliha Ayata said, “We are in the midst of a very important process. For approximately 50 years, the Kurdish people have resisted despite all kinds of heavy costs and suffering and have reached this point. As Kurdish women, we can say that a major struggle began years ago under the leadership of women. They took the lead in creating a new life and a new way of thinking. Despite all the shortcomings at this point and the fact that expectations have not been fully met, significant efforts have been made. Under the leadership of Mr Öcalan, and with the support of the peoples, a very important process is being carried out. The struggle and the character of the Kurdish people’s struggle are very different. Why? Because women are at the forefront of this struggle. Today, women from every people see themselves as part of this struggle.”


‘We are hopeful about peace and democracy’


Saliha Ayata said that women’s freedom is one of the fundamental objectives of the struggle. “The law adopted today is opening up a space in which everyone who has been obstructed and subjected to pressure can express themselves. The Kurdish people have for many years tried to express themselves despite various attacks and pressures,” she said. Ayata continued: “Today, the framework is becoming clearer through the paradigm of women’s freedom. As women, we are very hopeful; we are hopeful for both peace and democracy. This process is not an ending for us, but a new beginning. This struggle gives all of us hope, both for freedom and for an ecological life. Women are also following this process with great hope.”


‘Women are the leading force for peace’


Saliha Ayata said that women’s fundamental demands are the freedom of peoples and women, as well as equal citizenship. “With the steps to be taken after this one, both women and the Kurdish people must be able to live within democracy. Women must also have a place in this important process. We express this in every sphere. As we have said from the very beginning, women are the subjects of this process and the leading force for peace,” she said.


‘The process must not be carried out from a male-dominated perspective’


Saliha Ayata said that women’s demands must be reflected in every area of life, adding: “These demands must be implemented both in everyday life, in politics and in prisons. Women’s freedom must be taken as the basis. Peace and negotiation processes must not be conducted from a militaristic, sexist and male-dominated perspective, but through an approach in which women are the founding subjects. The next legal steps must be taken with this idea in mind.”

title: Swedish Foreign Minister: Process between Turkey andPKK  must continue peacefully and democratically
content:
The PKK’s decision to dissolve itself and the process being conducted with Turkey were brought before the Swedish Parliament. During the parliamentary session, developments concerning the opposition, free media, civil society and the rule of law in Turkey, as well as the process aimed at resolving the Kurdish question, were discussed.


In a written question addressed to Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard, Social Democratic Party MP Carina Ödebrink, from the main opposition party, said that the situation in Turkey had deteriorated further in recent months with regard to the opposition, free media, civil society and the rule of law.


Ödebrink noted that Turkey had failed to fulfill its obligations concerning the cases of Selahattin Demirtaş and Osman Kavala despite decisions by the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) and the Council of Europe. She asked what initiatives the Swedish government would take within the EU and the Council of Europe to ensure that Turkey complies with the principles of the rule of law.


Ödebrink also raised the question of whether a more coordinated position would be adopted at EU level to support democratic civil society, free media and human rights defenders in Turkey, and to oppose restrictions on the democratic rights of the opposition and civil society.


‘Peace must open the door to democratic reforms’


Speaking during the session, Social Democratic MP Kadir Kasırga said that Turkey was going through a historic turning point. Kasırga said that the identity, language and political rights of Kurds in Turkey had been denied for many years, adding that more than 40 years of armed conflict between the Turkish state and the PKK had cost tens of thousands of lives.


Kasırga said that the current process had created significant hope for ending the armed conflict and stressed that Sweden should support the process. Emphasising that peace means more than simply silencing the guns, Kasırga said that Kurdish identity, language and political rights must be guaranteed. He said that one of the fundamental tests of the process would be whether the peace process would pave the way for democratic reforms and whether people would be able to exercise their right to organise politically without fear while expressing their identities.


Kasırga argued that while a historic hope for peace was emerging in Turkey, democracy was deteriorating, saying that opposition politicians were being deprived of their freedom and that journalists and human rights defenders were being arrested.


Kasırga said that one way for Turkey to demonstrate that it wanted to open a new chapter would be to comply with ECHR rulings and release Selahattin Demirtaş, Figen Yüksekdağ and Ekrem İmamoğlu.


Stating that the transition “from conflict to peace, from denial to recognition, and from repression to democracy” must take place together, Kasırga asked whether the Swedish government viewed the peace process as an opportunity for the democratisation of Turkey as well.


Stenergard: We are closely monitoring the process


Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard said, in response to the MPs’ statements and the written question, that they were closely monitoring political developments in Turkey. Stenergard said that the government takes the deprivation of opposition figures of their freedom in Turkey very seriously, adding that freedom of expression, democracy, the rule of law and respect for the European Convention on Human Rights are of vital importance.


Maria Malmer Stenergard said: “I want to state that the government has long taken the latest domestic political developments in Turkey, including the deprivation of opposition figures of their freedom, very seriously. Respect for the European Convention on Human Rights, including the principles of freedom of expression, democracy and the rule of law, is absolutely vital. And, of course, it is also a prerequisite for EU membership. Citizens must be able to trust that courts reach independent and impartial decisions, rather than decisions based on the country’s existing anti-democratic laws, evidence that has yet to be proven, political interests or pressure. And therefore, let me be very clear.


A strong and independent judiciary is both a fundamental pillar of the rule of law and democracy, and a fundamental requirement for EU membership. For this reason, it is very important that Sweden and the EU clearly uphold their expectations of Turkey, particularly as an …

title: Karayılan: Shortcomings in the 'Framework Law' must be addressed
content:
Murat Karayılan, member of the People's Defense Central Command, issued a message in which he also addressed the latest developments within the scope of the Peace and Democratic Society process. He described the 'Framework Law' adopted by Parliament on 10 August as a new and important step, but said it contains serious shortcomings that must be addressed if the current process is to lead to a lasting peace.


The senior commander said about the current political developments: "On August 10th, the Turkish Grand National Assembly (TBMM) passed the Framework Law, something new in the history of the Republic. Since the Republic's founding, it has never recognized Kurdish will and instead sought to annihilate Kurds through killing. Seen in this light, this law is a new and valuable step. But this law has many deficiencies and errors.


Above all, it fails to include the architect of this process, Önder Apo [Abdullah Öcalan]. Yet it is Önder Apo who initiated this process. Likewise, the word "Kurd" doesn't even appear in it. Democracy is never mentioned at all. Our people's sensitivities, our movement's views, and even our Leadership's views have barely been taken into account. The matter has been reduced simply to the guerrilla laying down arms. Yet this is a century-old, immense problem. There is a narrow approach here. Without doubt, this narrow approach cannot bring the problem to resolution. As a result of what did the guerrilla emerge onto the stage of history? If this isn't properly unpacked, there can be no root-and-branch solution to the problem either.


On the other hand, in his first call, [Nationalist Movement Party leader] Devlet Bahçeli said of Önder Apo: "Let him stop the war, dissolve his organization, come to parliament, speak in the DEM Party group, and let the right to hope be fully recognized for him." Indeed, we based our Dissolution Congress decisions on exactly this. That is, we said "the process needs to be led by Önder Apo." We are saying the same thing now. The process needs to be led by Önder Apo. In other words, Önder Apo needs to have his physical freedom. Without this, nothing works."


Karayılan added: "I said before, "if Önder Apo is in prison, I cannot tell anyone to lay down their weapons and leave." I stand in the same place now. But now I can say this: "Dear comrade, go — Önder Apo will receive you. He will give you the perspectives for this new period." That is, if Önder Apo becomes actively involved, receives our comrades, holds meetings, and persuades them, then it can happen. We are ready to move this struggle off the ground of war and weapons and onto the ground of politics and law. Our Leadership has been working toward this for 33 years, and we trust him for it. The war waged over these 33 years was an excessive war — one that, in truth, was not in its proper place to begin with. But we were forced to wage this war against those who sought to annihilate us. It has always been this way. We want to bring this war to an end, and that is our sincere approach.


What did Önder Apo say about this process? He said: "We moved from the gallows to the dialogue table. This can be the beginning, the first step, of an important process." This is highly significant. That is how we approach it too. But if the architect of this process is in prison, this won't work. Everyone needs to know this. I believe state officials know this too. Because this is the truth."


Karayılan continued: "On the other hand, the language being used still hasn't changed. The language of war was clear before; it was the Turkish state's language of war, its language of psychological warfare. They kept saying, "We struck and we won." When the August 15th Offensive took place, Turkey's president was Kenan Evren. Kenan Evren said: "Whoever commits this crime, whatever hole they've crawled into, whatever rock they've hidden under, our army will grab them by the ears within 72 hours and bring them before justice." Yet that 72 hours has now become 42 years, and it still hasn't happened. Önder Apo set out alone. Now we are millions; we have tens of thousands of cadres. Who has won, who has lost? This people, once on their deathbed, now stand on their feet. They are the most freedom-oriented, democratic, and combative people in the region. They are the hope of all peoples when it comes to building a democratic and free system founded on women's liberation. This is what August 15th created: it created a national spirit …

title: Iran executes Shahram Sadeghi
content:
Executions continue in Iran. Shahram Sadeghi was detained and arrested in Karaj for taking part in the January protests.


The Karaj Revolutionary Court sentenced Sadeghi to death and ordered the confiscation of all his assets for an “operational act” under Article 1 of the Law on the Aggravation of Punishment for Espionage and Cooperation with the Zionist Regime and the United States and hostile groups against national security and interests.


His lawyers appealed to Iran’s Supreme Court. Following the Supreme Court’s approval of the sentence, Shahram Sadeghi was executed this morning.


According to information published by Mizan, the Iranian judiciary’s news agency, Sadeghi’s assets were confiscated.


The report did not provide information on where Sadeghi was executed.

author: Jan Klauth /Die WELT
title: „Fuck Künstliche Intelligenz!“ – Amerikas Hass auf KI
content:
Aus Ablehnung gegenüber KI und Angst vor Arbeitslosigkeit wächst in den USA die Protestbewegung gegen die Tech-Konzerne. In der Regel bleiben die Proteste friedlich – doch eine Welle der Gewalt verunsichert das Silicon Valley.


Vor dem New Yorker Firmensitz von Palantir wird es laut. Eine Gruppe von Demonstranten hat zu Sprechchören gegen die „Agenda von Big Tech“ angesetzt, dann tritt Claire Valdez ans Mikrofon. Die 36-jährige Politikerin vom Linkaußen-Flügel der Demokraten brüllt beinahe ins Megafon. „Voller Zorn“ sei sie hierhergekommen, sagt sie.


„Wir stehen auf gegen diese schreckliche Technologie und die Milliardäre, die davon profitieren“, ruft Valdez. Der Protest der Gruppe „Make the Road New York“ richtet sich an diesem heißen Donnerstag gegen drei Dinge: die Datensammlungs-Software von Palantir, die Einsätze der ICE-Agenten – und gegen den Bau neuer Rechenzentren. Landesweit finden diese Woche mehr als ein Dutzend Kundgebungen statt.


Dabei läuft alles geordnet und friedlich ab. Aber das ist nicht immer so. Denn mit der zunehmenden Skepsis gegenüber den großen Tech-Firmen ist die Stimmung im Land gekippt. Laut einer Umfrage des Forschungsunternehmens Gallup lehnen mittlerweile sieben von zehn Amerikanern den Bau von Rechenzentren in ihrer Region ab. Kaum ein Viertel befürwortet solche Projekte, wobei sich lediglich sieben Prozent stark dafür aussprechen. Und nicht nur Menschen aus dem linken politischen Spektrum lehnen die Bauvorhaben überwiegend ab. Auch unter Anhängern der Republikaner ist eine Mehrheit gegen den Bau der Anlagen in Wohngebieten.


Mit dem stetig wachsenden Einsatz von KI, aber auch der normalen Nutzung des Internets, steigt der Bedarf an Rechenleistung unaufhörlich an. Überall im Land sind Rechenzentren geplant oder im Bau. Denn Präsident Donald Trump will den KI-Wettlauf gegen China gewinnen und hat für die Branche ein erhebliches Subventionsprogramm aufgesetzt. Mittlerweile stehen laut Branchendaten der Analysefirma Aterio mehr als 2000 große Datenzentren im ganzen Land, 809 befinden sich derzeit im Bau – und hunderte weitere sind in Planung.


Beim Protest gegen die Bauvorhaben geht es nicht nur um eine „Not-in-my-backyard“-Mentalität („Nicht in meinem Garten“). Längst hat sich die Bewegung gegen Big Tech als Ganzes gerichtet. Vor allem junge Amerikaner haben Angst vor dem Jobverlust – oder davor, umsonst Unsummen in eine Universitätsausbildung gesteckt zu haben, die ihnen schon bald nichts mehr bringt.


Denn zwar boomen die Tech-Konzerne und mit ihnen die amerikanische Wirtschaft. Aber am Arbeitsmarkt kommt davon nichts an. Aktuelle Zahlen zeigen einen klaren Trend zum Stellenabbau statt zu Neueinstellungen – vor allem getrieben durch die KI. Hauptverantwortlich für den Großteil des Stellenabbaus sind Oracle, Amazon, Dell und Meta, jeweils mit Zehntausenden gestrichenen Stellen. Allein in Kalifornien fielen seit Jahresbeginn laut dem Tracking-Portal layoffs.fyi mehr als 16.000 Tech-Arbeitsplätze weg, etwa ein Fünftel davon bei Meta.


Tech-Firmen erhöhen Sicherheitsstandards


Vielerorts hat sich das Gefühl eingeschlichen, dass, wer bei Meta, Microsoft und Co. codet, an nicht weniger als der Abschaffung des eigenen Jobs arbeitet. Schon länger hat sich auch an den Universitäten des Landes der Wind gedreht. Auf den großen Hype im Zuge des KI-Siegeszuges folgte Ernüchterung.


Immer wieder nutzen prominente Akteure aus Politik und Wirtschaft ihre Reden anlässlich der Abschlussfeiern, um für die KI-Revolution zu werben – und ernten dafür klare Ablehnung. Die Immobilienmanagerin Gloria Caulfield etwa teilte den Absolventen der University of Central Florida mit, dass „der Aufstieg der Künstlichen Intelligenz die nächste industrielle Revolution“ sei. Die Reaktion war lautes Buhen.


Musikproduzent Scott Borchetta, Chef des Musiklabels Big Machine Records, wurde an der Middle Tennessee State University verhöhnt, als er sagte, KI stelle die Musikbranche auf den Kopf. Auch die Rede des ehemaligen Google-CEOs Eric Schmidt an der University of Arizona ging in Buhrufen unter. Frenetischen Beifall erntete hingegen der Comedian Ronny Chieng, der Studenten in Harvard zurief: „Fuck Künstliche Intelligenz! Die Mission eurer Generation ist es, KI zu zerstören.“


Einige Protestler haben Aufforderungen wie diese wohl sehr wörtlich interpretiert. Neben legitimen Protesten kommt es in den USA zunehmend zu Gewaltaktionen und Anschlagsversuchen. Für Aufsehen sorgte etwa das, was sich im April in der …

author: Anonym
title: NACH DEM JULI
content:
Wir nehmen uns die Zeit, die Lage ein wenig zu entwirren und einige Überlegungen zum 25. Juli und zu den Angriffen auf die TAV-Baustelle zu teilen.


Wir haben uns entschlossen, in einer öffentlichen Debatte das Wort zu ergreifen, die wir als hoffnungslos feindselig, orwellsch und unempfänglich für Fakten empfinden, denn es erscheint uns notwendig, inmitten eines Meeres aus Täuschungen und Rhetorik etwas Aufrichtiges zu sagen. Eine beißende und giftige Rhetorik, unabhängig davon, wie sie sich präsentiert.


Die vorherrschende Variante dieser Rhetorik ist die Propaganda der Repression mit ihren verschiedenen Nuancen: Verwüstung und Plünderung, internationale Gewaltprofis, terroristische Bedrohung. Es erscheint wirklich sinnlos, Worte zu verschwenden, um darauf zu antworten, wo jedes Wort seine Bedeutung verliert und sich sogar ins Gegenteil verkehrt. Wer genau wird denn eigentlich terrorisiert? Welcher Gewaltprofi agiert bei einer Massendemonstration, an der Hunderte von Menschen beteiligt sind, über eine Stunde lang, bei der Erstürmung einer Baustelle und dem darauf folgenden Kampf?


Der einzige offensichtliche Wille zur Terrorisierung geht von einer ideologischen, polizeilichen und staatlichen Maschinerie aus, die der Generation, die sich auf den Straßen für Gaza politisiert hat, eine klare und unmissverständliche Botschaft senden will: Versucht es nicht noch einmal. Auf der Straße zu kämpfen, der Polizei Widerstand zu leisten, kann euch extrem teuer zu stehen kommen.


Das Echo, das von links kommt, steht dem in nichts nach. Wer erst in den letzten Jahren die ersten Schritte im Widerstand gegen diese Welt der Katastrophen unternommen hat, muss eine ständige Domestizierung durch Trauma und Drohungen erdulden. Ein Ausnahmezustand folgt auf den nächsten, ein ferngesteuertes Massaker und ein Polizeimord folgen aufeinander, mit dem daraus resultierenden Schock und dem Gefühl der Ohnmacht. Doch all das reicht nicht aus: Hinzu kommt noch der erpresserische Befehl, stets in den Reihen zu bleiben, um die Lage nicht zu verschlimmern, nicht „die nützlichen Idioten der Rechten“ zu sein und den gefährlichen Abstieg in den Polizeistaat nicht zu beschleunigen. Verantwortungsbewusst sein und damit unterwürfig sein. Dabei wird schamlos ignoriert, dass gerade diese feige Anpassung an alle auferlegten Maßnahmen der Regierungen, an alle offiziellen Versionen, die uneingeschränkte Achtung vor der Autorität – sei sie politischer, wissenschaftlicher, kultureller oder polizeilicher Natur – in jeder Hinsicht das Wiederaufleben der Faschisten begünstigt hat.


Und die Linke trägt die Hauptverantwortung dafür, trotz ihrer unsachlichen Schmähreden gegen diejenigen, die den Mut und die Klarheit zeigen, die ihr selbst immer gefehlt haben.


Die wenigen Bilder dieses Tages haben alle gesehen: eine Rauchsäule, die aus einem brennenden Kleintransporter aufsteigt, pyrotechnische Effekte, ein Regen aus Steinen, die Baustelle in Trümmern.


Etwas ganz anderes ist es, aus nächster Nähe mitzuerleben, wie sich die Polizei in ungeordneter Flucht zurückzieht, wie eine Menschenmenge die Baustellenabsperrungen stürmt und überwindet, wie sich die Euphorie unter allen Anwesenden ausbreitet – sowohl unter den Jugendlichen, die ihre ersten Erfahrungen machen, als auch unter den erfahrenen Genossen.


Die Empfindungen, die solche Momente hervorrufen, tragen dazu bei, gegenseitiges Vertrauen aufzubauen und Bindungen zu knüpfen, die dadurch Gestalt annehmen, dass man gemeinsam ein Risiko eingeht, sich gegenseitig beschützt, die Angst auf die Probe stellt und sie im Kampf überwindet. An dieser Erfahrung ist nichts Episches oder Kriegerisches, sondern eine unmittelbarere Auseinandersetzung mit der eigenen gemeinsamen Verletzlichkeit und vor allem die Entschlossenheit, diese gemeinsam zu überwinden, sich zu exponieren und die Niederlage abzuschütteln. Kein Kult der Stärke also, aber auch keine selbstmitleidige Faszination für die eigene Ohnmacht.


Deshalb läuft die Vereinfachung, Etiketten zu produzieren, um die Fakten in Schubladen zu stecken, ins Leere, ganz gleich, ob ihr Ziel darin besteht, zu legitimieren oder zu kriminalisieren. Es ist ein Vorgehen, das die politische Kraft des Bruchs neutralisiert, indem es ihn auf das Symptom von etwas anderem reduziert, sei es Öko-Angst oder internationale Inszenierungen. Und deshalb muss es bekämpft werden.

title: Mobi für die Rheinmetall Entwaffnen Proteste in Köln und Hamburg
content:
Das Protestcamp in Köln vom 01. – 06. September 2026 und die Aktionstage in Hamburg 24. – 26. September 2026 sind die zentralen Protestaktionen von Rheinmetall Entwaffnen. Dort wollen wir unsere antimilitaristische Praxis stärken und uns der weltweiten als auch deutschen Aufrüstung entgegenstellen.


Du möchtest zu den Protesten gegen Rheinmetall und Aufrüstung nach Köln oder Hamburg fahren? Dann komm am Montag, 24. August 2026, 19:30 Uhr ins NewYorck Bethanien, Berlin-Kreuzberg.


Bei Backwaren und Salat informieren wir über die Proteste in Köln sowie Hamburg, verkaufen Busticket für die An- und Abreise und es wird ein Buchtisch der Schwarzen Risse zum Thema Antimilitarismus geben. Im Anschluss wird Raul Zelik ein Vortrag über den Zusammenhang zwischen globaler Faschisierung und deutscher Aufrüstung halten mit anschließendem Q&A.


Wann: Montag, 24. August 2026, 19:30 Uhr.


Wo: NewYorck Bethanien, Mariannenplatz 2a, 10999 Berlin-Kreuzberg, 2. Etage.

19:30 Uhr: Ankommen bei Salat und Backwaren


20:00 Uhr: Infos zum Protestcamp in Köln und zu den Aktionstagen in Hamburg


20:15 Uhr: Vortrag von Raul Zelik mit Q&A

title: Xerîb Hiso: Mam Zekî’s role as a leader was very valuable and historic
content:
PYD Co-Chair Xerîb Hiso spoke about the life and struggle of Mam Zekî Şengalî (İsmail Özden), a member of the KCK Executive Council and the Êzidî (Yazidi) Coordination, on the eighth anniversary of his death.


Beginning his remarks by commemorating Mam Zekî Şengalî and all those who were killed in the Turkish state’s airstrike on Shengal on 15 August 2018, PYD Co-Chair Xerîb Hiso said: "Eight years have passed since the death of Mam Zekî Şengalî. Yet, the Yazidi society continues its struggle on the basis of the spirit of resistance created by martyr Mam Zekî. Why was Mam Zekî targeted? Why was his death timed to coincide with the day commemorating the Koço massacre? 15 August was the day when ISIS gangs entered Shengal, surrounded the area around the village of Koço and carried out a massacre. All of this has political and historical significance. In particular, there was a specific reason why Mam Zekî was targeted and killed that day.


 


Our Yazidi society has always followed in the footsteps of its leaders; there is a bond between the sheikhs, pirs and the people. This is how society has been preserved. There are also many writers and intellectuals among the Yazidis. There are researchers and historians. Those who lead societies have always been targeted. Well-known figures such as Mirza Destanî and Mam Zekî were deliberately killed. I met Mam Zekî two years before his death. We met in 2012. I was very happy. We met in Sulaymaniyah. I was very curious to meet and see Mam Zekî. When we saw each other, I felt as though we had known each other for a very long time. Perhaps we had things in common in terms of our ideas and the spirit in which we lived. Physically, however, each of us was in a different place. But when we met, I did not feel any sense of unfamiliarity."


Hiso added: "Our friendship was very new, but intellectually we shared the same views; we were part of the same cause and struggle, and complemented one another in terms of our movement and ideas. Although we had never met before, we established a genuine comradeship. We were very happy at that meeting. Later, we met and visited one another several times. We went to Shengal many times and saw each other there as well. Mam Zekî would say, ‘We are also Yazidis; we need to visit Yazidi society and give them morale. Şengal needs this.’ So we went to Shengal once again. All the PADÊ comrades from Shengal were there. They held a ceremony and welcomed us warmly. We wanted to celebrate Çarşema Sor in Serdeşt. But the KDP security forces did not allow us to go to Serdeşt and prevented the celebration from taking place."


Drawing attention to Mam Zekî’s leading role within the Yazidi society, PYD Co-Chair Xerîb Hiso continued: "Mam Zekî’s role within the Yazidi society was very valuable and historic. Mam Zekî knew the movement in Europe and was the father of martyr Sipan. There were many resistance fighters and martyrs in his family. When he joined the struggle in Europe, he was arrested because he had adopted the revolutionary line. Imprisonment also meant torture. When he was released, he went directly to the free mountains. Just as he had organised the Yazidi society in Europe, he began organising the Yazidi society in Southern Kurdistan as well. Our Êzidî society had great trust in Comrade Zekî. After the genocide, great trust also developed in all the comrades who came to Shengal to liberate it and carried out work there. The Yazidi society’s love and respect for Comrade Zekî was immense. That is why they called him ‘Mam’.


Mam Zekî would visit every home, every sheikh and every leader, and saw society as a whole. He worked day and night for the Yazidi society. Comrade Zekî was a revolutionary, a patriot, an intellectual and a knowledgeable person; his role within the Yazidi society was immense. Not only the Yazidis of Shengal, but all Yazidis living in other parts of Kurdistan and outside Kurdistan knew Mam Zekî’s moral strength and ideas. Everyone knew him. When Shengal was attacked and a massacre was carried out there, the first leading comrade to step forward was Comrade Zekî. Dozens and hundreds of guerrillas, as well as YPG-YPJ forces, headed towards Shengal. A very dangerous massacre had taken place. Children and men had been killed and women had been abducted. Koço was one of these villages. Those who managed to survive the massacre reached Mam Zekî."

Partî bi navê vegerandina hêvî û hêzê bo gelê Kurdistanê di serdemeke dijwar û giran de hate damezrandin. title: DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti, Selahattin Demirtaş ve Selçuk Mızraklı'yı ziyaret etti
content:
DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti üyeleri Pervin Buldan ve Mithat Sancar, eski HDP Eş Genel Başkanı Selahattin Demirtaş ve eski Diyarbakır Büyükşehir Belediye Eş Başkanı Adnan Selçuk Mızraklı'yı Edirne Cezaevi'nde bugün ziyaret etti.


Heyetten yapılan açıklamada, şunlar kaydedildi:


"Arkadaşlarımızın morali yüksekti, herkese selamları vardı. Süreci, cezaevi koşullarının elverdiği ölçüde yakından takip ettiklerini söylediler. Görüşmede arkadaşlarımıza çerçeve yasa ve süreçte gelinen aşama hakkında bilgi verdik, onların değerlendirme ve önerilerini aldık.


Arkadaşlarımız, çerçeve yasanın TBMM'den büyük bir destekle çıkmış olmasının çok değerli olduğunu, yasanın uygulanması için tüm tarafların üzerine düşeni yapacaklarına inandıklarını belirttiler. Sürecin sağlıklı işleyebilmesi açısından herkesin katkı sunmasının büyük bir önem taşıdığına vurgu yaptılar.


Her zaman ifade ettiğimiz üzere arkadaşlarımız, özgürlüklerinden artık bir saat bile mahrum kalmamalıdır. Bu hem adaletin hem de sürecin doğasının gereğidir. Demirtaş ve cezaevindeki diğer siyasetçilerin yıllardır maruz kaldığı bu hukuksuzluğun giderilmesi, hele de çerçeve yasanın kapısını araladığı bu yeni dönemde, hepimizin ihtiyacı olan barış ve demokrasinin tesis edilmesine önemli bir katkı sunacaktır."

title: Aslan: Despite the law’s shortcomings, let’s insist on further steps toward democratization
content:
The Framework Law entitled “Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” which had been expected as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, passed the General Assembly of Parliament with 467 votes in favor, 87 against and 7 abstentions.


The 12-article Framework Law has been the focus of criticism because it contains no steps toward democratization. DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan, one of the lawyers of Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan, spoke to ANF and said that the law should be regarded not as a final outcome but as a new beginning.


“The approach of placing disarmament before democratization is still in place”


Evaluating the 12-article bill prepared for the resolution of the Kurdish question, DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan began by saying that the Framework Law, described as a transitional law, does not fully meet expectations. Recalling that the legislation falls short of the inclusiveness required by the process, Newroz Uysal Aslan said:


“We expected a much more comprehensive and much clearer transitional law for the Peace and Democratic Society Process to move forward. Although the process is rhetorically described as a Turkish-Kurdish alliance and Turkish-Kurdish brotherhood, the introductory section setting out the rationale for the Framework Law shows that the state’s security-oriented approach has not fundamentally changed. The approach of treating disarmament as a precondition for democratization steps continues. The language of the law still contains old concepts and approaches from the state’s bureaucratic and political vocabulary, which shows that a process of complete transformation has not yet begun. Although the spirit of the law is based on the logic of ‘ending conflict and transitioning to politics,’ it contains controlling mechanisms at certain points that could obstruct political activity. Perhaps we cannot describe it entirely as the old security-oriented mindset, but legally it still bears traces of a controlling and restrictive approach. They justify this by referring to social concerns and sensitivities, but these sensitivities are often interpreted one-sidedly. From the perspective of the Kurdish people or those who want democracy, the law of course failed to meet expectations when viewed not through the lens of ‘the internal front’ or ‘national survival,’ but from the perspective of democracy and the law of peace.”


“THE NSC IS NOT A MECHANISM THAT WILL OVERSEE THE ENTIRE PROCESS!”


Addressing the debate over the role assigned to the National Security Council (NSC) under the law, Newroz Uysal Aslan said that the NSC is not the sole mechanism responsible for overseeing the entire process. Explaining that the NSC is essentially positioned as a mechanism for determining and confirming that weapons have been laid down, Newroz Uysal Aslan said:


“The NSC is not the mechanism that will oversee this entire process. In other words, it is not the mechanism that will conduct the legal procedures or carry out postponement and monitoring processes. The determination that the PKK has dissolved itself and that weapons have been laid down will be made by the National Intelligence Organization and state institutions, while the NSC will play a role in the confirmation process provided for by the law following that determination. The supreme board that will be established following the NSC decision, comprising eight ministries including the Office of the Vice President, the Ministries of Justice, Interior and National Defense, will be the executive mechanism responsible for implementing the 12 articles of the Framework Law. There will also be a parliamentary monitoring and follow-up committee.”


“THEY ARE TRYING TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF STATUS DE FACTO, WITHOUT INCLUDING IT IN THE LAW”


While the state’s executive mechanism has broad powers, there has been debate over the limited powers of the body to be established with political representation under the law. They insist that this mechanism was adopted because the application process is limited during the first six months. But this approach is problematic. Because they are establishing a supreme board that is closed to political and civil mechanisms. They say that we can make appointments within it, conduct hearings and establish subcommittees. And this will happen. But there is no commitment or clear guarantee as to how civil, impartial or independent these bodies will be. For example, the supreme board does not …

title: Bakırhan: This law is not an end, but a beginning
content:
DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan made assessments on current developments at the 3rd Ordinary Congress of the Aydın Provincial Organization.


At the beginning of his speech, Bakırhan said: "Hopefully, in the coming days we will also bring the DEM Party paradigm to Aydın." He added: "In Aydın, as in every corner of Turkey, we will be a home, a place for everyone seeking justice, seeking peace, seeking equality, and wanting their language, identity and beliefs to be free."


 


This law is not an end, but a beginning


Stating that the DEM Party is the party of Börklüceli, Torlak Kemal and Şeyh Bedrettin, Bakırhan said the following regarding the framework law: "These are historic days. The framework law has enabled us to cross a threshold where weapons and violence are removed from the equation and we can now discuss our issues on a legal and political basis. But this law is not an end, because it is the first step. The law itself is not the democratic solution to the Kurdish question. The law itself does not grant Alevis legal recognition of their right to equal citizenship. This is simply a law that removes the basis of violence and places the issue on a legal and political footing. So this law is a beginning, not an end. This law is not one in which the Kurdish people's language and identity are dissolved. This is not a law in which the Alevi people's right to equal citizenship is eliminated. This law is a new beginning. With this law, we will organize more strongly and struggle more strongly.


We are entering a new period in which the Kurdish language will be free, in which the languages of all the peoples living in Turkey will be free; in which all beliefs, especially Alevis, will be able to express themselves freely and equally; in which there will be no bloodshed or conflict and young people will not lose their lives; in which the farmers, tradespeople and people of Aydın will receive what they are entitled to for their products and their labour. Yes, we struggled, we paid a heavy price and we have reached this point. A table has been established, and the Kurdish question is being discussed at this table. We should not underestimate this. The establishment of this table is itself of historic importance. For the first time, the Kurdish question has found a place on the parliamentary agenda and, with a law, has effectively entered the parliamentary record. Therefore, this law is not an end but a beginning.


Our people ask, ‘What did we gain with this law?’ This is not a law about giving and taking. This law stopped violence and bloodshed. We have crossed the threshold into a struggle that will secure our language, identity, culture, democratic rights and legal protections through democratic struggle, without weapons or conflict, through democratic means and methods. That is why this congress is important. That is why our congresses are important. Hopefully, by expanding the struggle, we will together achieve results worthy of our labour and our values."


Peace has no losers


Bakırhan added; "There is no winner or loser in peace. Peace is a good thing. Peace brings abundance. Peace is beautiful. There are people in Turkey who oppose the peace process and criticize it. Of course, there are aspects that can be criticized. But believe me, negotiations in which people do not lose their lives are in the interests of this country and of our 86 million people. They are in the interests of tradespeople and workers in Aydın. They are in the interests of our villagers and farmers who cannot receive a fair return for what they produce. Why? Just yesterday, government officials stated in Parliament that 2.5 trillion dollars had been spent on this environment of conflict and violence. Do you know what 2.5 trillion dollars means? It means building six schools instead of one school in Aydın, six hospitals instead of one hospital, six health centres instead of one. It means finding jobs for six people instead of one. In other words, with this process, the country's resources will go not to conflict and war but to workers, pensioners, the poor, farmers, fig producers, cotton producers and tobacco producers. That is why we say at every opportunity that this process concerns all 86 million people. This is not a Hakkari, Şemdinli, Şırnak or Siirt process; it is a Turkey-wide process. With peace, we will all be able to breathe more easily. With peace, this country's resources will not be squandered. The country's resources …

author: Unknown
title: Süleymancılara operasyon: Cemaatin lideri Alihan Kuriş tutuklandı
content:
Süleymancılar cemaatine yönelik Ankara Başsavcılığı tarafından "çıkar amaçlı suç örgütü" iddiasıyla yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında 13 Ağustos Perşembe günü düzenlenen operasyonda gözaltına alınan cemaat lideri Alihan Kuriş, tutuklanarak cezaevine gönderildi.

Başsavcılık, 13 Ağustos’ta "Alihan Kuriş çıkar amaçlı suç örgütü" soruşturması kapsamında 49 kişi hakkında gözaltı kararı vermişti. Operasyon kapsamında 37’si gözaltına alınmıştı.

6 soruda Süleymancılar: Süleymancılar kimdir? Neden hedef oldular?

Soruşturmanın "suç örgütü kurma ve yönetme", "suç örgütüne üye olma", "suçtan kaynaklanan mal varlığı değerlerini aklama", "kamu kurum ve kuruluşları zararına dolandırıcılık" ve "vergi usul kanununa muhalefet" iddialarıyla yürütüldüğü açıklanmıştı.

Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınan Alihan Kuriş’in adli işlemleri tamamlandı. Kuriş, çıkarıldığı mahkeme tarafından tutuklanarak cezaevine gönderildi.

Süleymancılara yönelik soruşturmada hangi şirketlere operasyon düzenlendi?

Diğer şüphelilere ilişkin adli sürecin ise devam ettiği belirtildi.

Cemaate yönelik soruşturma kapsamında "kara para aklama" faaliyetlerinde kullanıldığı öne sürülen aralarında Ayakkabı Dünyası'nın da yer aldığı 32 şirkete ve mal varlıklarına kayyım atanmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: MasterChef şampiyonu Eren Kaşıkçı’nın ölüm nedeni belli oldu
content:
Gastronomi yarışması MasterChef Türkiye'de 2021 yılında şampiyon olan ve geçen ay İstanbul'daki evinde ölü bulunan Eren Kaşıkçı'nın ön otopsi raporu tamamlandı. Adli Tıp Kurumunda (ATK) yapılan ön incelemelerde 37 yaşındaki şefin ölümün kalp krizi kaynaklı olduğu belirlendi.

“Kızılsakal” lakabıyla tanınan Eren Kaşıkçı, 29 Temmuz'da Sarıyer'deki evinde ölü bulunmuştu. Uzun süre kendisine ulaşamayan ortağı Mikail B.'nin eve gelmesiyle Kaşıkçı'nın hayatını kaybettiği anlaşılmıştı.

ATK'de yapılan incelemelerin ardından hazırlanan ön otopsi raporuna göre, bilinen kronik bir rahatsızlığı bulunmayan Kaşıkçı'nın kalp krizi sonucu yaşamını yitirdiği belirlendi.

Sözcü'de yer alan habere göre, cansız bedeni üzerinde yapılan incelemelerde Kaşıkçı'nın bulunmasından yaklaşık 14-15 saat önce hayatını kaybettiği değerlendirildi.

Kaşıkçı'nın ölümüne ilişkin soruşturma henüz tamamlanmadı. Ölüm nedenine ilişkin kesin değerlendirme, Adli Tıp Kurumu tarafından hazırlanacak nihai raporun soruşturma dosyasına eklenmesinin ardından netleşecek.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Türkiye'ye getirilen Serkan Kurtuluş tutuklandı
content:
Türkiye'de işlediği çeşitli suçlar nedeniyle hakkında kırmızı bülten çıkarılan suç örgütü elebaşı Serkan Kurtuluş, Arjantin'deki iade sürecinin tamamlanmasının ardından Türkiye'ye getirildi. Kurtuluş; "tasarlayarak öldürme", "kasten öldürme", "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma", "tehdit", "nitelikli yağma", "tehlikeli maddeleri izinsiz olarak bulundurma veya el değiştirme", "suç işlemek amacıyla kurulan örgüte üye olma" ve "silahla yağma" suçlarının da aralarında bulunduğu 33 suçtan aranıyordu.

İzmir Başsavcılığınca 2017'de hazırlanan ve İzmir 3. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesince kabul edilen iddianame kapsamında Kurtuluş'un SEGBİS üzerinden ilk ifadesi alındı. Yaklaşık 10 yıldır yurt dışında yaşadığını belirten Kurtuluş, mevcut davayla bağlantılı olarak Arjantin'de 6 yıl 2 ay, Gürcistan'da ise 8 ay tutuklu kaldığını söyledi.

Suçlamalar ve dava konusu hakkında bilgi sahibi olmadığını savunan Kurtuluş, Türkiye'deki ceza kanunlarına göre tutukluluk süresinin 5 yılı geçemeyeceğini öne sürerek tutuksuz yargılanmasını talep etti. Cumhuriyet savcısı ise mevcut delil durumu, isnat edilen suçların niteliği ve kaçma şüphesi nedeniyle Kurtuluş'un tutuklanmasını istedi.

Mahkeme heyeti, soruşturmanın başından bu yana firari durumda olan ve atıl suçları işlediğine dair kuvvetli olgular bulunan Kurtuluş'un tutuklanmasına karar verdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Danilo Arao
title: Marikina
content:
Locals walk and run along Gil Fernando Ave. Extension, Marikina City. Photo from Marikina PIO's Facebook page

Kumpara sa ibang lugar sa Metro Manila, totoong masayang manirahan sa Marikina. Pero kailangan pa ring ipaglaban ang pag-unlad para sa karamihan.

Sadyang masayang manirahan sa tinaguriang Shoe Capital ng Pilipinas.

Siyempre’y maraming sapatos na mapagpipilian. Mas mura sa palengke pero mayroon din naman sa mga mall. May sariling gusali rin ang mga “sosyal” na tatak tulad ng Otto at Rusty Lopez. Siyempre’y mas mahal ang sosyal. Mas matibay ba ang mahal kumpara sa mura? Simple lang ang sagot: May sorpresang resulta sa matiyagang pag-iikot sa palengke!

Pero higit pa sa sapatos ang Marikina. Malinis ang paligid sa pangkalahatan. Medyo maluluwag ang mga bangketang nalalakaran. Sa katunayan, ang siyudad ay para sa mga mahilig maglakad o magbisikleta. Kaya huwag magulat kung maraming residenteng gumigising nang maaga para mag-jogging o mag-biking.

Sa oras ng almusal, tanghalian, hapunan o kahit simpleng meryenda, may mapupuntahan ang mga tinatamad magluto sa bahay. Napakarami kasing makakainan, lalo na sa kahabaan ng mga kalyeng Lilac at Gil Fernando. Lutong Asyano, Amerikano o Europeo? May mapagpipilian ang kahit maselang panlasa kaya dinarayo ang mga kainan sa Marikina lalo na kung payday. Pero may isang putaheng malamang na magpapangiti sa tinaguriang tunay na Marikenyo: Everlasting.

Hindi perpekto pero sinisikap na maging inklusibo. May mga kalyeng hindi man masyadong maluwag ay may bicycle lanes naman. May mangilan-ngilan ding kalyeng para lang sa bisikleta.

Kahit na mayroon pa ring sumusuway sa mga alituntunin, may sistema pa rin naman sa iba’t ibang bagay tulad ng waste management, street parking at traffic flow. Kapansin-pansin ang maayos na sistema noong panahon ng pandemya dahil may sapat na impormasyong ipinamahagi sa bakuna at ayuda. At ngayong tag-ulan, maayos din naman ang isinagawang evacuation sa mga apektadong lugar.

Ang wagas na binabaha noon, hindi na masyadong malala ngayon. Pero may pagbaha pa rin sa ilang lugar, lalo na sa pinamamahayan ng mahihirap. Ligtas na ang Provident Villages na inabot hanggang bubong ang baha noong 2009. Pero panibagong problema sa lugar na ito ang planong pagpuputol ng maraming matatandang puno para magtayo ng isang tulay. Buti na lang at tinutulan ito ng maraming residente.

“Cherished ecological treasures” ang terminong ginamit ng isang opisyal ng homeowners association. Kung sabagay, hindi dapat kinokompromiso ang kapaligiran kapalit ng diumanong kaunlaran. Sino ba kasi ang makikinabang sa kaunlarang kinokompromiso ang ekolohiya ng lugar? Hindi ba’t layunin lang ng mga mayaman ang lalo pang magkamal ng yaman?

May ganito ring isyu sa isang malaking mall sa Marikina na nagbukas halos 10 taon na ang nakaraan. Maraming punong nawala para itayo ang mahigit 10,000 square meters na estruktura. Inireklamo rin ng maliliit na negosyante ang paghina ng suplay ng tubig, bukod pa sa pangkabuuang paghina ng negosyo. Sa katunayan, maraming nagsara dahil nalugi. Mayroon mang pikit-matang kumuha ng puwesto sa malaking mall, napilitan ding umalis dahil hindi nakayanan ang napakataas na renta.

Muli, para kanino ba ang tulay, mall at iba pang estrukturang nagreresulta sa pagkawala ng mga puno’t halaman? Kahit na may ginagawa naman ang pamahalaang lokal para panatilihin ang mga lumang parke, kailangan pa ring mapigilan ang pagsasamantala ng mga mayaman at makapangyarihan.

May bahagi ng Gil Fernando na sinasara tuwing Linggo ng umaga para makapaglaro ang mga bata at makapag-Zumba ang mga hindi na. Pero mula Lunes hanggang Sabado, nariyan pa rin ang trapik at usok mula sa sanlaksang sasakyan. Ang kalahating araw na kasiyahan ng pamilya ay pansamantalang pagtakas lang sa araw-araw na kalbaryong bunga ng mapagkunwaring pag-unlad.

Kumpara sa ibang lugar sa Metro Manila, totoong masayang manirahan sa Marikina. Pero kailangan pa ring ipaglaban ang pag-unlad para sa karamihan.
