title: Frauen unter der Herrschaft der Taliban in Afghanistan kämpfen für ihre Rechte
content:
Dossier


Wie im Iran vermischt sich auch in Afghanistan der Widerstand von Frauen mit dem ethnischer Minderheiten und sozialen Problemen. Besonders die Gruppe der Hazaras wird von den Taliban verfolgt und ermordet. Darunter sind auch viele Frauen, die dem Regime Widerstand leisten wie Marzia und Hajar Mohammadi. Die beiden Freundinnen wurden am 30. September 2022 mit weiteren 60 vor allem Frauen und Mädchen durch ein Sprengstoffattentat auf ein Bildungszentrum für Frauen in Kabul ermordet. Das Selbstmordattentat löste Proteste von Frauen in ganz Afghanistan aus. Der Anschlag ereignete sich in Dasht-e Barchi, einem Gebiet in Kabul, das überwiegend von Angehörigen der schiitischen Hazara-Gemeinschaft bewohnt wird. Am 3. November 2022 hat die Taliban zudem eine Konferenz von Frauenrechtsaktivist:innen im gleichen Viertel gestürmt und u. a. Zarifa Yaqubi festgenommen. Wir wollen hier die Proteste sichtbar machen, die auch durch die

aktuelle iranische Bewegung

 inspiriert werden, aber auch die Lebensbedingungen der Frauen und Mädchen schildern:


Vor 5 Jahren haben Frauen in Afghanistan fast alle Rechte verloren, nun sind weibliche Journalistinnen und Verfechterinnen der Frauenrechte besonders im Visier der Taliban


Afghanistan: Taliban lassen sechs Menschenrechtsaktivisten gewaltsam verschwinden. Stiftung für Rechtsforschung zur dringenden Befreiung von Frauen und Kindern


„

Die Taliban-Behörden in Afghanistan haben sechs Mitarbeiter der Nichtregierungsorganisation

Women and Children Legal Research Foundation


 (WCLRF) seit fast einem Monat gewaltsam verschwinden lassen, teilte Human Rights Watch heute mit.


Die Taliban haben keine Angaben zum Verbleib der Führungsspitze der Organisation gemacht, die am 18. Juli 2026 in Kabul festgenommen wurde. Die „Women and Children Legal Research Foundation“ führt Hilfsprogramme durch und betreibt Forschung und Interessenvertretung im Bereich der Frauen- und Kinderrechte. Die Taliban-Behörden sollten Familienangehörigen und Rechtsbeiständen den Besuch der Inhaftierten gestatten, und diese sollten unverzüglich freigelassen werden, sofern ihnen keine anerkannte Straftat zur Last gelegt wird. (…)


Am 21. Juni führten Sicherheitskräfte der Taliban eine Razzia im Büro der „Women and Children Legal Research Foundation“ in Kabul durch und beschlagnahmten Laptops und Mobiltelefone von Mitarbeitern. Eine gut informierte Quelle berichtete Human Rights Watch, dass die Sicherheitskräfte das Büro durchsuchten, es versiegelten und in den folgenden Wochen Mitarbeiter zu ihrer Arbeit befragten.


Am 18. Juli wiesen Taliban-Vertreter sechs männliche Mitarbeiter an, zum Büro der Organisation zurückzukehren, um ihre beschlagnahmten Geräte abzuholen. Stattdessen wurden alle sechs in Gewahrsam genommen. Angehörige der inhaftierten Männer gaben an, dass die Taliban-Vertreter keinerlei Informationen über ihren Verbleib, ihren Zustand oder etwaige gegen sie erhobene Vorwürfe bereitgestellt hätten.


„Ihre Familien leben in ständiger Angst und Unsicherheit“, sagte Zarqa Yaftali, die ehemalige Leiterin der Stiftung, die nun eine Schwesterorganisation in Kanada leitet. (…) Vertreter der Taliban haben keine Angaben zu den Gründen für diese Festnahmen gemacht. Allerdings haben sie schon seit langem weibliche Journalistinnen, Verfechterinnen der Frauenrechte und Frauen, die für ihre Rechte demonstrieren, ins Visier genommen. Viele von ihnen wurden willkürlich festgenommen und inhaftiert, sind gewaltsam verschwunden – manchmal wochenlang –, wurden unter missbräuchlichen Bedingungen festgehalten und gefoltert

…“ engl.

Pressemitteilung vom 13. August 2026 von Human Rights Watch


 (maschinenübersetzt)


Ein Albtraum


„

Am 15. August jährt sich die Rückkehr der Taliban an die Macht zum fünften Mal. Im Interview berichtet Chakawak Kawiani über den Tag, der Afghanistan und ihr Leben dramatisch verändert hat. Die 21-jährige Chakawak Kawiani kam im vergangenen Jahr mit ihrer Mutter und ihren drei jüngeren Brüdern über das Bundesaufnahmeprogramm aus Pakistan nach Deutschland. Ihre Mutter war Teil eines Untergrundnetzwerks in Kabul, das sich mit medico-Unterstützung für Frauenrechte einsetzte und dies noch immer tut. Als die Gefahr zu groß wurde, tauchte die Familie erst unter und floh dann nach Pakistan, wo sie fast eineinhalb Jahre in ständiger Sorge vor Razzien und der Ablehnung der deutschen Behörden auf die Ausreise wartete. medico unterstützte die Familie in dieser schwierigen Phase. Heute lebt …

author: Corey Larocque
title: Nunavut needs auditor general’s help on drinking water
content:
News that Canada’s auditor general is going to take a look at Nunavut’s drinking water should be welcome news to all Nunavummiut. To all Canadians, in fact.


Across the territory, there’s a lot that doesn’t seem to be going right with the supply of drinking water. At the same time, governments are pumping a lot of money into improvements to water and sewage infrastructure.


Nunavummiut

learned this week

 the auditor general is going to do an audit of the management of Nunavut’s drinking water, expected to be published next year.


A little advice from the auditor general should help identify what changes need to be made as well as shine a light on the way public money is being spent.


Canada’s auditor general Karen Hogan is the independent officer of Parliament responsible for conducting audits and studies of federal and territorial public institutions.


You might recognize her name from such audits as this year’s review of the Family Services Department’s

handling of children in care

 and last year’s

Public Housing in


Nunavut

 report that pointed to a lack of transparency in the territory’s plan to build 3,000 homes between 2022 and 2030.


Provinces have their own auditors general, but because Nunavut doesn’t have one, the federal official is responsible for reviewing territorial institutions and offering advice to the legislative assembly.


Governments sometimes bristle at auditor general reports because they frequently point out the shortcomings of governments or public institutions.


In recent years, there has been a litany of water problems in Nunavut. (The details are laid out in a

story

 by reporter Nehaa Bimal about the upcoming auditor general’s report on page 7 of this week’s paper).


Water woes have been experienced by people in Arctic Bay, Baker Lake, Coral Harbour,

Gjoa Haven

,

Iqaluit,


Kugaaruk

, Naujaat,

Pangnirtung

, Pond Inlet, and

Sanikiluaq

.


In 2024, a Nunatsiaq News

story

 reported only eight of Nunavut’s 25 water treatment plants had passed their most recent public health inspections without health or safety deficiencies.


Adverse conditions in Nunavut’s drinking water have ranged from short-term boil water advisories because of the risk of contamination due broken infrastructure to do not consume orders to states of emergency.


In some cases — such seawater getting into Kugaaruk’s water treatment plant or diesel fuel contaminating Iqaluit’s supply — the military has been called in to distribute bottled water or to use its specialized equipment normally used in disaster areas to purify water.


When you need the military to step in and provide clean drinking water in communities of 1,300 or 8,700, there’s a serious problem.


The federal government is spending a lot of money to improve Nunavut’s water infrastructure. The biggest, highest-profile project is the $214 million in funding then-prime minister Justin Trudeau announced to upgrade Iqaluit’s water infrastructure.


A 2023 Drinking Water Strategic Framework estimated the cost of addressing the territory’s water treatment needs at $605 million.


Everyone knows there’s a huge need to improve Nunavut’s drinking water supply. There’s a lot of money needed, and already a lot of money flowing.


That’s why the thoroughness of an auditor general’s review of the situation is good news for Nunavut.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Milei es el espejo: así quiere verse la ultraderecha española
content:
Camaradas, cada vez que Javier Milei abre la boca en Buenos Aires, en Madrid alguien toma nota. Milei no es una anomalía sudamericana, es el laboratorio. Es el espejo donde el PP, VOX, Santiago Abascal, Isabel Díaz Ayuso y Alberto Núñez Feijóo se miran para saber hasta dónde pueden llegar cuando el pueblo baja la guardia.


Argentina toca fondo una y otra vez, y cada vez cae más bajo. No podía ser de otra manera con un vendepatrias en el Gobierno, un lacayo que alinea la política exterior y económica de su país a los intereses de Washington antes que a los de su propio pueblo. Milei y sus Libertos son el hazmerreír del mundo, sí, pero también son una amenaza muy seria para la clase trabajadora argentina, que es quien paga la broma.


La gran estafa de la “libertad”


A Milei le encanta presentarse como un adalid de la libertad, un “anarcocapitalista” que venía a demoler los privilegios de la casta. Esa fue, desde el minuto uno, la gran estafa. Quienes defendemos los derechos de los de abajo sabemos que para el neoliberalismo más extremo la palabra “libertad” significa una sola cosa: libertad de los poderosos para explotar sin límites, y sálvese quien pueda para el resto.


La supuesta “casta” contra la que Milei prometía luchar nunca fueron los grandes empresarios ni los fondos buitre. La verdadera casta que su gobierno decidió aplastar es la clase trabajadora con derechos: obreros que pierden su empleo, pensionistas desamparados, familias que ya no pueden alimentar a sus hijos mientras desmantelan la sanidad y la educación públicas. Milei solo le gusta a quien tiene la barriga llena.


El fracaso que abre la puerta.


El verdadero peligro de personajes mesiánicos como Milei es que no surgen de la nada. Son el resultado monstruoso del fracaso de una falsa izquierda institucional que abandonó la calle, que se dedicó a la política de salón y que le abrió las puertas de par en par a la extrema derecha. Cuando un pueblo se siente desprotegido y carece de una vanguardia organizada, es fácil engañarlo con discursos de odio y promesas vacías.


Argentina es hoy una lección dolorosa para toda la clase obrera mundial: nos muestra lo que ocurre cuando un pueblo pierde la conciencia de clase. Sin conciencia colectiva ni organización sindical, nos dominan fácilmente. La dolarización, la privatización de todo lo público y el fin de las ayudas a los más pobres no son “reformas”, son una máquina de generar miseria que arrastra al país hacia el abismo.


El “PPVOX” en España: el mismo guion.


Alberto Núñez Feijóo representa la continuidad del modelo privatizador que ya ensayó en Galicia, camuflado bajo una falsa apariencia de moderación gestora. Esa centralidad se desmorona en cuanto se analiza su dependencia total de los sectores más duros de su partido y de la extrema derecha para sostener gobiernos autonómicos y locales.


Isabel Díaz Ayuso es el ariete del neoliberalismo salvaje, el motor ideológico del ala más desacomplejada de la derecha. Su gestión en Madrid es el ejemplo vivo del populismo identitario como cortina de humo: mientras agita discursos de confrontación permanente, ejecuta el deterioro sistemático de la sanidad, la educación y los servicios sociales públicos, entregando los recursos comunes a fondos buitre y grandes corporaciones.


Santiago Abascal y VOX operan como la punta de lanza de la reacción: su función es radicalizar el debate público, normalizar el discurso de odio y cuestionar los derechos de minorías y mujeres. Ese extremismo no es anecdótico, sirve para desviar la atención de los problemas materiales de la gente y romper la conciencia de clase mediante el chovinismo.


El “PPVOX” no es un eslogan, es una realidad material: regalos fiscales a las rentas más altas, privatización encubierta de la sanidad y la dependencia, y oposición frontal a cualquier avance en derechos laborales o vivienda. Su objetivo no es gobernar para la ciudadanía, sino blindar los privilegios de las élites financieras a costa de empobrecer a la mayoría social.


Y Junts per Catalunya, que se presenta como oposición al centralismo español, tendrá que explicar algún día cómo pretende sostener en el poder a los mismos que aplicaron el artículo 155 y reprimieron el derecho de autodeterminación en Catalunya. VOX y PP comparten con Junts las mismas políticas económicas antiobreras; lo que los separa es el modelo de Estado, no la defensa de la clase trabajadora, que en ninguno de los tres casos existe.


La respuesta es la …

author: subMedia auf Deutsch
title: Was ist Eigentum?
content:
Alle Machtstrukturen sind in Ideologien verwurzelt. Der gemeinsame Glaube an diese Ideologie ist es, der diese Machtstrukturen aufrechterhält. Im Kapitalismus ruht das Gebäude der sozialen Kontrolle auf der kollektiven Illusion des Privateigentums und der Unantastbarkeit des sogenannten „freien Marktes“. Jeder Versuch, diese Logik in Frage zu stellen, wird daher Gegenwehr seitens der indoktrinierten Befürworter des Systems hervorrufen und mit Sicherheit die Aufmerksamkeit der repressiven und reaktionären Staatsbeamten auf sich ziehen. Aber wie das Sprichwort sagt … man kann kein Omelett machen, ohne ein paar Eier zu zerbrechen. Und man kann den Kapitalismus definitiv nicht stürzen, ohne sich in die Sachen der Leute einzumischen.


Also … was ist Eigentum überhaupt? Und was haben Anarchisten dagegen?

author: anred
title: El Gobierno de la Ciudad restringió el XXII Mathapi Apthapi Tinku: las actividades se desarrollan hoy en Parque Los Andes
content:
La Dirección General de Permisos y Ferias autorizó el uso del espacio público únicamente para la jornada de este sábado, desestimando la solicitud original de tres días consecutivos. La Comisión Organizadora fue notificada ayer por la tarde. El cronograma para el día domingo se informará en las próximas horas.

Por Mario Wilmer para ANRed

 


La 22° edición del encuentro cultural Mathapi Apthapi Tinku comenzó a desarrollarse durante la mañana de hoy en el Parque Los Andes, en el marco de una disposición del Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires que redujo la autorización del evento a una sola jornada.


A través de una resolución oficial, la Dirección General de Permisos y Ferias otorgó el permiso de uso del espacio público exclusivamente para este sábado 15 de agosto, en la franja horaria de 12:40 a 20:00 horas. La medida gubernamental desestima el pedido de la organización, que había tramitado el espacio para los días 14, 15 y 16 de agosto.  


El documento detalla que la restricción responde a que la Junta Comunal Nº 15 prestó conformidad únicamente para la fecha del sábado. La disposición habilitó el inicio del armado de la infraestructura a las 08:00 horas de hoy y establece como límite para el desarme las 22:00 horas de esta misma jornada.  


El conflicto por la utilización del predio mantiene antecedentes recientes. Con tiempo anticipado la Comisión Organizadora presentó una solicitud de intervención institucional, señalando que la Dirección de Permisos y Ferias había esgrimido como impedimento para el permiso la programación de una actividad propia de la Comuna 15 en la misma fecha y lugar. En dicho reclamo, las comunidades recordaron que el encuentro se realiza en el parque desde hace veintiún años de forma ininterrumpida y que fue declarado de Interés Cultural por la Legislatura porteña en 2025.  


Ayer viernes, durante el desarrollo de las actividades ceremoniales en honor a los difuntos, María Pomacusi, integrante de la organización, ayer contó en las redes sociales de la organización públicamente la recepción de la disposición: «Hoy a las 6 y media de la tarde nos llega la notificación oficial donde nos permite solo el sábado».


Sobre el proceso del trámite, Pomacusi detalló: «En un primer momento dieron el permiso, avanzamos con los requerimientos de permisos y ferias y faltando 10 días nos dijeron que la Comuna decidió otorgar el permiso el día sábado. Lamentamos esta decisión porque mantuvimos mucho diálogo y asumimos compromisos, el Mathapi desde la comisión organizadora pagó todo lo que necesitábamos para este evento».


Las declaraciones apuntaron a la gestión local: «Tenemos una profunda preocupación y un repudio a la decisión que tomó el Gobierno de la Ciudad en las manos del presidente de la Comuna 15, Agustín Rodríguez Conti, quienes no lograron entender la magnitud que implica la 22° organización del encuentro de Sikuris del Mathapi Apthapi Tinku».


Desde el espacio cultural ratificaron el desarrollo del cronograma previsto para el día de hoy. «Llamamos a todos a que acompañen el Mathapi, a que sigamos difundiendo y repudiando esta decisión autoritaria y violatoria de los derechos de los pueblos indígenas en la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, a nivel provincial, nacional e internacional», expresó Pomacusi ayer por la tarde.


Respecto a las actividades que estaban pautadas originalmente para mañana, la comisión organizadora definirá la nueva modalidad y locación durante el transcurso de la jornada.

author: Randi Beers
title: The winter dark
content:
In 1903 Knud Rasmussen was experiencing his first taste of life in the far north of Greenland, a winter adventure that would change his life and draw him back to the Inughuit — the Polar Inuit — time and time again.


One fall day, on his way back to the hut that expedition members had built and in which they would pass the winter, he happened upon an old woman who stopped him and pointed out over a calm sea to a black bank of fog that shrouded the horizon.


“Out there over the sea,” she said dolefully. “It is the dark coming up, the great dark!”


The Inughuit live farther north than any other Inuit. In Qaanaaq, where I spent a few winters in the 1980s, the sun disappears for 120 days. If a new moon should happen to roughly coincide with the winter solstice, then the darkest period of a long winter is dark indeed.


Greenlanders have a name for this sunless period: kaperlak (you might see it written as kaperdlak if you are reading something written in an old account). It is a word that describes the dark time, the winter night north of the Arctic Circle, for south of that unseen line the sun does not disappear completely.


In far northern parts of Canada, too, there is a word, tauvikjuaq, which means “the great darkness.” 


Suersaq – or Hans Hendrik as he was known to non-Inuit – was a Kalaaleq – a Greenlander from below the Arctic Circle – who first went to the High Arctic with an American explorer, Elisha Kent Kane, in 1853.


His home was on the approximate latitude of Iqaluit, but he passed that first winter north of present-day Qaanaaq. To put this in a Canadian context, it is quite a bit farther north than Grise Fiord. 


Suersaq’s first dark season terrified him. One of the few Inuit to leave a memoir from that time, he wrote, “Then it really grew winter and dreadfully cold, and the sky speedily darkened. Never had I seen the dark season like this, to be sure it was awful, I thought we should have no daylight any more. I was seized with fright, and fell a weeping. I never in my life saw such darkness at noon time. As the darkness continued for three months, I really believed we should have no daylight more. However, finally it dawned, and brightness having set in, I used to go shooting hares.”


Contrast those observations of a West Greenlander newly-arrived in the far north, with the observations of the Inughuit themselves, as recorded by Rasmussen.


He saw that people of the far north, like people everywhere, like change.


Poetically, he wrote, “When, a whole summer through, your eyes have been bathed in light day and night, you long to see the land vanish softly into the darkness again, that the stars and the moon may light their lamps.”


The Inughuit lived lives circumscribed by the sea and the icecap. In the summer they were confined to the relatively narrow strip of land that separated these two predominant features of their geography. The coming of the polar night meant the coming of an ice surface on which to travel.


“Now the dark nights are coming,” the men told Rasmussen, “soon the ice will close in the sea! Be glad, for soon blubber lamps shall light those who go out to fetch meat from the flesh-pits! And windows and fires shall light far out in the night, and hasten the lagging pace of late-returning sledges!” 


To the Inughuit, the people of the far north, the polar night was liberating. They celebrated all the good things it would bring: the frozen sea, hunting on the ice, sled-trips after bears and, for the men, a respite from the sweltering houses.


And soon enough it would end and usher in a glorious spring time of increasing light, when the sea surface was still frozen and the hunter’s world expanded. 


Taissumani is an occasional column that recalls events of historical interest. Kenn Harper is a historian and writer who lived in the Arctic for over 50 years. He is the author of 

Give Me Winter, Give Me Dogs: Knud Rasmussen and the Fifth Thule Expedition

, and 

Thou Shalt Do No Murder

, among other books. Feedback? Send your comments and questions to kennharper@hotmail.com.

author: Unknown
title: PJAK: August 15 initiative saved the existence and dignity of the Kurdish people from annihilation
content:
The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) issued the following statement on the 42nd anniversary of the August 15 initiative, which marks the beginning of the PKK’s armed struggle in Turkey.


The PJAK statement on Saturday includes the following:


“Forty-one years have passed since the historic initiative of August 15, 1984, which marked the great resurgence of our people in the face of wars and policies of genocide. On the 42nd anniversary of this historic epic, which saved the existence and dignity of the oppressed Kurdish people from annihilation, we respectfully commemorate all the martyrs of this struggle.


Several decades ago, this initiative, launched under the leadership of Commander Egîd from the village of Dihî in the Eruh district in Bakurê (Northern) Kurdistan, brought the oppressed Kurdish people’s four-decade-long relentless struggle closer to the stage of full freedom. The initiative, which began against the Republic of Turkey and a century of oppression against peoples, particularly the Kurdish people, spread across all four parts of Kurdistan.


The fascist Turkish regime published an image of a gravestone on the summit of Mount Ararat, which had become a symbol of the Kurdish people’s resistance and struggle, bearing the words: “Here lies the imaginary Kurdistan.” This was a period in which a nation-state, from the moment of its birth, embarked on a horrific process of genocide against the Kurds. For more than a century, it carried out dozens of massacres, destroyed villages and the environment, subjected Kurds to forced displacement, while the international community remained silent in the face of these acts.


The Kurdish people, however, never accepted this. The struggle that emerged among the Kurds against waves of fascism and massacres became—and continues to be—a liberation struggle that has helped shape the path to freedom for oppressed peoples across the Middle East.


Undoubtedly, the Treaty of Lausanne and massacres such as Dersim, Anfal, and Halabja were all carried out along this trajectory. The Kurds made history through dozens of major uprisings, demonstrating extraordinary sacrifice and resistance. Exactly 42 years ago, guided by the perspectives of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan], under the command of Martyr Egîd, and through the sacrifices made in the Kurdish struggle for freedom, the first shot was fired, and its echo of freedom continues to resonate to this day.


This initiative shook fascism to its core. At a time when the Turkish nationalist government felt secure in its efforts to eliminate the Kurds, the August 15 initiative served as a warning to all fascist forces that had shed the blood of our people across the four parts of Kurdistan. It opened a new chapter in history, bringing the Kurds onto the historical stage with greater prominence and proclaiming before the eyes of the world that the struggle for freedom is always possible when sustained by hopes and aspirations for a better future.


With a powerful cry, that shot broke the silence of the international powers and superpowers that, through agreements such as Lausanne, had paved the way for the emergence of Turkey and the region’s genocidal nation-states, confronting them with a major challenge.


From that point onward, the mountains that were intended to become a graveyard for the Kurds suddenly turned into arenas of struggle and symbols of liberation. The initiative launched by Commander Egîd was not merely a military undertaking, but an epic rooted in the manifesto of a people’s path to freedom—one that disrupted the scenarios devised by the world’s superpowers. August 15 effectively brought an end to the scenario of dividing Kurdistan into four parts; the path of “Berxwedan Jiyane” (“Resistance is Life”) began and continues resolutely today with the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (“Woman, Life, Freedom”) revolution.


The initiative of the Kurdish freedom movement became a fundamental source of support for the peoples of the Middle East and a symbol of their determination. In the past, Leader Apo initiated systematic struggle as a method for the resurrection of a people; today, we see its repercussions across global society and in the international arena. In this way, the process of genocide and assimilation was confronted with successive defeats, and the Middle East benefited from these gains.


Today, at a more advanced stage, the August 15 initiative offers hope for a democratic society and a democratic nation shaped …

author: Unknown
title: Women’s Revolution Council established in Iran
content:
The Women’s Revolution Council in Iran, comprising a group of women activists working in the fields of politics, civil society, media, women’s rights, and human rights, officially announced its formation today.


The statement on Saturday emphasized that the Council was established with the aim of strengthening women’s political power and organizing their independent, effective, and decisive presence in the country’s public and political spheres. Defending the right to life and opposing the death penalty are also among the Council’s objectives.


According to the statement, five women take the lead in establishing the Women’s Revolution Council: Samaneh Sevadi, Sanam Devletshahi, Mina Khani, Naimeh Dostdar, and Yasemin Fahede.


The Women’s Revolution Council stated: “We operate as a democratic, pluralistic, inclusive, and feminist network. Women in Rojhilatê (Eastern) Kurdistan and Iran have for decades been at the forefront of the struggle against Iran’s rulers, gender discrimination, and patriarchal mentality. However, the fundamental issue—the demand for women’s genuine and decisive participation in structures of power and political decision-making—has yet to change.”


The statement stressed that women are still not adequately represented in political structures, alliances, and processes in which decisions about the country’s future are made; that their presence remains merely symbolic; and that women should make up at least 50 percent of decision-making bodies.

author: Unknown
title: 15 August: History’s verdict
content:
In recent days, almost everyone has spoken. Those who have encountered the Kurdish question at some point in their lives have spoken, as have those who have watched it from afar, those who have paid a price and those who have paid no price at all. Politicians, lawyers, journalists, former and current actors, those who support the process, those who oppose it, those who are hopeful and those who are doubtful have all had their say. What has emerged is a strange picture: a text that has been talked about so extensively actually has very little to say when viewed on the historical scale of the Kurdish question.


Perhaps this is why we now need to talk a little less about the law. Because the real issue is not whether a legal regulation consisting of a few articles is good or bad, but within what historical framework the Kurdish question, which has lasted for more than a century, and the Kurdish freedom struggle, which has lasted for more than fifty years, should be understood. The moment we begin to assess a great historical accumulation formed around the claims of independence, freedom and the right to determine one’s own future through the limited instruments of current politics, we not only misread the present, we also diminish the scale of the past.


This is precisely where we need to look at 15 August. It is not a history that can be confined to any legal text, negotiation process or temporary political balance. It is one of the founding moments that reorganised the modern historical memory of the Kurds. Nor is it the only such moment. Şêx Said, Agirî-Zîlan, Dersim, Anfal, Raperîn, Kobanê and Aleppo, although they took place in different periods, in different parts of Kurdistan and under very different circumstances, are historical thresholds at which the Kurds were forced to rethink their own political existence, destiny and visions of the future. What brings these moments together in a shared historical memory is not that they resemble one another, but that in different periods and in different parts of Kurdistan they reshaped the Kurds’ sense of existence, will and vision of the future.


The distinctive character of 15 August within this continuity is clear. Following the great ruptures experienced after the founding of the Republic, the long period of silence, the 12 September regime and Diyarbakır Prison, the new Kurdish generation carried its claim to intervene in its political future through its own will into a new phase with this date. For this reason, defining 15 August merely as a military beginning is insufficient to explain the political and sociological transformation it created within Kurdish society.


The meaning that 15 August carries today is greater than current politics precisely for this reason. Politics is limited by today’s balance of power, law by the existing state order, and negotiations by the conditions in which they take place. Historical memory cannot be entirely contained by any of these. The meaning of 15 August cannot be determined by a law passed today, a negotiating table established tomorrow, or a political strategy that may change on another day. That meaning has already been formed through its consequences over more than forty years, the society it transformed, the political subject it created and its place in modern Kurdish history.


Precisely for this reason, what needs to be focused on today is not so much the legal text itself as the historical meaning attributed to it. In the past, the Republic of Turkey also resorted to various legal instruments under the headings of surrender, repentance, reintegration into society and effective remorse. Their scope and techniques were not the same; it would not be correct to present today’s regulations as a simple repetition of those of the past. Yet a change in legal technique does not eliminate the question of within which political and security paradigm an issue is being defined.


Presenting a limited transitional regulation emerging after forty-two years of an extremely heavy period of conflict as carrying a historical meaning far beyond its own legal capacity creates a serious problem of scale. The question here is not whether the law is sufficient or insufficient, but the political discourse that enables a limited legal instrument to be perceived almost as the founding document of a new historical era.


The further the real capacity of a legal text becomes separated from the historical meaning attributed to it, the more …

author: Unknown
title: HPG and YJA Star guerrillas: We will continue to walk in the footsteps of commander Egîd
content:
The 14 July resistance was undoubtedly an epic resistance that raised the flag of victory. Commander Egîd (Mahsum Korkmaz) knew this very well. For this reason, he said, “Whatever happens, the 14 July resistance must be crowned with a great offensive.” On this basis, he organised the 15 August offensive with a flawless plan and strategy. The 15 August offensive was launched simultaneously in Dihê (Eruh) and Şemzînan (Şemdinli), two of the most strategic areas of the cities of Bakûr. 15 August became the day of rebirth for the Kurdish people. At the same time, it became a symbol of the war for freedom alongside Commander Egîd. Today, the HPG and YJA Star guerrillas, who are welcoming the Resurrection Holiday with great enthusiasm, say they are determined to continue their march towards truth by following in the footsteps of the great commander Egîd.


 


Saluting Abdullah Öcalan, the Kurdish people and their comrades on the Resurrection Holiday, guerrilla Selcan Mehran said: “Indeed, 15 August is a very meaningful and important day. Because the Kurdish people were facing the threat of annihilation. Thousands of brave people emerged in Kurdistan in the person of Comrade Egîd. As guerrillas, we too act in the spirit of 15 August and follow in the footsteps of Commander Egîd. The 15 August offensive launched under the leadership of Comrade Egîd inspired all Kurdish young people to rise up. We need to look at the situation of the Kurdish people before 15 August and the level they reached with the 15 August offensive. As a militant of Rêber Apo [Abdullah Öcalan], I too take this line of resistance as my basis.”


Without 15 August, we would not exist


 


Guerrilla Bager Serhed, who spoke about the great importance of the 15 August offensive for the Kurdish people, said: “Even after a hundred years have passed, we will always keep this day alive, remember it and welcome it with enthusiasm. Because it is the 15 August offensive that gave us this spirit. The Resurrection Holiday created this spirit: the spirit of keeping alive, the spirit of resistance, the spirit of struggle. Undoubtedly, this developed under the leadership of Comrade Egîd. It is also necessary to mention Comrade Egîd’s commitment to the Leadership. They left us a legacy that enabled us to reach where we are today. We can say once again that if there had been no 15 August, our existence would also have been eradicated. There were signs of this. But after 15 August, the enemy’s calculations did not succeed. To say it once again, the 15 August offensive has great significance for us. We must never forget this, especially as the Kurdish people. Once again, we congratulate Rêber Apo and the Kurdish people on the Resurrection Holiday. We will always keep alive the spirit of 15 August created by Comrade Egîd.”


 


Guerrilla Avzem Cûdî said: “Through Comrade Egîd, a new way of thinking and a legend were created. At a time when the Kurds were being denied, Comrade Egîd launched an offensive,” and added: “This offensive enabled the rebirth of the Kurds and brought about an awakening among the Kurdish people. The courage of the Kurds had been broken, their will had been broken. At such a time, a commander like Comrade Egîd turned towards Botan. He laid the foundations for the establishment of the guerrilla army and carried out actions. He enabled the Kurdish people to feel their own strength again. As a guerrilla from Botan, we grew up with the legendary stories of Comrade Egîd. What makes Commander Egîd a legend today is his stance and personality. In addition to this, it is his commitment to Rêber Apo. Today, the HPG and YJA Star forces follow in the footsteps of Comrade Egîd. We came to know guerrilla warfare through Comrade Egîd. Because before I was born, my mother and father had stayed together with Comrade Egîd. On this occasion, I once again congratulate Rêber Apo and all the comrades on the Resurrection Holiday.”

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Bakunin’in Siyaset Felsefesi: I. Kısım — FELSEFE
content:
Çeviren: Scianus


 I. Bölüm — Dünya Görüşü


[NOT: Paragrafların başında kalın harflerle yazılı alt başlıklar Maksimov’un eklemeleridir; geri kalan kısımlar Bakunin’e aittir.]

Doğa Aklın Zorunluluğudur

. Varlığın mahiyetine dair felsefî tartışmalara burada girişecek değilim. Tabii, Doğa sözcüğünü sık sık kullanmak mecburiyetinde olduğumdan, onunla ne kastettiğimi açıkça ortaya koymam gerekir.

“Doğa, gerçekten var olan şeylerin toplamıdır,” diyebilirdim. Lâkin böylesi bir tanım bize son derece cansız bir Doğa tasavvuru verirdi; oysa Doğa bize tam tersine, bütünüyle yaşam ve hareket olarak görünür. Kaldı ki şeylerin toplamı nedir? Bugün var olan şeyler yarın aynı hâlde bulunmayacaktır. Lâkin yok olup gitmeyecekler; yalnızca başka biçimlere dönüşeceklerdir. Bu sebeple eğer şöyle dersem hakikate daha yakın düşmüş olurum: Doğa, bağrında durmaksızın meydana gelen ve gelmeye devam edecek olan bütün dönüşümlerin toplamıdır. Bu bütünlük fikrini daha belirgin kılmak adına şu önermeyi temel bir ilke olarak ortaya koyuyorum: 

Var olan her şey; evrenin o sınırları tayin edilemez bütününü meydana getiren bütün varlıklar; dünyadaki her mevcut şey — nitelik ve nicelik bakımından ne kadar farklı yahut benzer olurlarsa olsunlar, ister büyük ister küçük, ister birbirine yakın ister uzak bulunsunlar — zorunlu olarak ve farkında olmaksızın birbirleri üzerinde, doğrudan yahut dolaylı, sürekli bir etki ve tepki icra ederler. Bu sayısız özel etki ve tepkinin, tek bir genel hareket içinde birleşmesiyle ortaya çıkan ve teşekkül eden şeye biz Yaşam, Dayanışma, Evrensel Nedensellik yahut Doğa adını veririz. Dilerseniz buna Tanrı da diyebilirsiniz Mutlak da. Bu adlandırmanın kendi başına hiçbir önemi yoktur. Yeter ki Tanrı sözcüğüne, burada belirlediğimiz anlamdan başka bir mânâ yüklenmesin: Gerçekten var olan tüm şeylerin birbirleri üzerinde aralıksız olarak icra ettikleri sonsuz sayıdaki etki ve tepkinin; önceden tasarlanmamış, kararlaştırılmamış, bilinmemiş; lâkin doğal, zorunlu ve gerçek olan evrensel bileşimi. İşte böyle tanımlandığında, Evrensel Dayanışma yahut sonsuz bir evren olarak düşünülen Doğa, kendisini zihnimize aklın zorunlu bir gereği olarak kabul ettirir.

1

Evrensel Nedensellik ve Yaratıcı Dinamik

. Şu açıktır ki bu Evrensel Dayanışma mutlak bir ilk neden niteliği taşımaz. Bilakis o, tikel nedenlerin eşzamanlı faaliyetlerinin meydana getirdiği bir sonuçtur; bu tikel nedenlerin toplamı zaten evrensel nedenselliğin kendisini teşkil eder. O yaratır ve daima yeniden yaratılacaktır. Var olan her şeyin kesintisiz dönüşümlerinin sonsuz toplamı tarafından sürekli yaratılan birleşik bir birliktir; lâkin aynı zamanda o şeylerin yaratıcısıdır da.  Her nokta Bütün üzerinde etkide bulunur —burada Evren ortaya çıkan sonuçtur— ve Bütün de her nokta üzerinde etkide bulunur — burada ise Evren yaratıcıdır.

Evrenin Yaratıcısı.

 Bu tanımı ortaya koyduktan sonra, herhangi bir belirsizliğe düşme korkusu olmaksızın şunu söyleyebilirim: Dünyaları yaratan şey Evrensel Nedensellik, yani Doğadır. Yerküremizin mekanik, fizikî, jeolojik ve coğrafî yapısını belirleyen odur. Yeryüzünü bitkisel ve hayvansal hayatın bütün ihtişamıyla donatan da odur. Ve bugün hâlâ, insan dünyasında, toplumun geçmişteki, bugünkü ve gelecekteki bütün gelişimlerini yaratmaya devam etmektedir.

2

Doğa Yasalara Uygun Davranır.

 İnsan, kendisini kuşatan ve kendi içinde de keşfettiği Doğa parçasını dikkatle ve uzun süre gözlemlemeye başladığında, sonunda bütün şeylerin kendi öz doğalarını meydana getiren içkin yasalar tarafından yönetildiğini fark edecektir. Her şeyin kendine özgü bir dönüşüm ve faaliyet biçimi vardır. Bu dönüşüm ve faaliyet içinde, aynı koşullar altında değişmeden tekrar eden olgular ve olaylar dizisi bulunur; buna karşılık yeni ve belirleyici koşulların etkisi altında bunlar yine aynı derecede düzenli ve belirli bir biçimde değişirler. Aynı nedenlerin etkisiyle aynı olguların sürekli yeniden üretilmesi, işte Doğanın yasama tarzı budur: olguların ve olayların sonsuz çeşitliliği içindeki düzen.

En Yüksek Yasa.

 Evren içerisinde işleyen, bilinen ve bilinmeyen bütün yasaların toplamı, onun tek ve en yüksek yasasını oluşturur.

3

Başlangıçta Eylem Vardı.

 Bu şekilde kavranan bir Evrende ne

a priori

 fikirler bulunabilir ne de önceden tasarlanmış ve buyurulmuş yasalar. Fikirler —Tanrı fikri de dahil olmak üzere— yeryüzünde yalnızca zihnin onları ürettiği ölçüde vardırlar. Dolayısıyla onların doğal olgulardan ve bu olguları yöneten yasalardan çok sonra …

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Bakunin’in Siyaset Felsefesi – Rudolf Rocker’ın Önsözü
content:
Çeviren: Scianus


MİHAİL BAKUNİN

, on dokuzuncu yüzyılın devrimci şahsiyetleri arasında eşsiz bir yere sahiptir. Bu sıra dışı insan, aynı kişilikte pek ender rastlanır biçimde, cesur bir toplumsal-felsefi düşünürü ile eylem adamını bir araya getirmişti. İnsan toplumunun herhangi bir alanını dönüştürmeye imkân verecek en küçük fırsatı dahi değerlendirmeye daima hazırdı.


Ne var ki, 1871 Paris Komünü’nün yenilgisinden sonra onun coşkun ve ateşli eylem arzusu bir nebze yatıştı; nihayet 1874’te Bologna ve Imola ayaklanmalarının başarısızlıkla sonuçlanmasının ardından, ölümünden iki yıl önce siyasî faaliyetlerden bütünüyle çekildi. Uzun zamandır mücadele ettiği hastalıklar, zaten güçlü bünyesini ciddi biçimde yıpratmıştı.


Lâkin onu bu karara sevk eden yalnızca bedenî kuvvetlerinin giderek tükenmesi değildi. Bakunin’in, sonraki hadiseler tarafından defalarca doğrulanan siyasî öngörüsü, 1870-71 Fransız-Prusya Savaşı’nın ardından yeni Alman İmparatorluğu’nun doğuşuyla birlikte Avrupa tarihinde bambaşka bir devrin açıldığına işaret ediyordu; ona göre bu yeni dönem, Avrupa’nın toplumsal gelişimi bakımından felaket getirecek ve toplumun sosyalizm ruhuyla yeniden doğuşunu hedefleyen bütün devrimci teşebbüsleri uzun yıllar boyunca felce uğratacaktı.


Dolayısıyla onun mücadeleyi bırakışı, hastalıktan harap düşmüş yaşlı bir adamın ideallerine olan inancını yitirmesinden kaynaklanan bir hayal kırıklığı değildi. Bilakis, savaşın doğurduğu yeni şartlarla birlikte Avrupa’nın, 1789 Büyük Fransız Devrimi’nin meydana getirdiği geleneklerden köklü biçimde kopan ve yerini şiddetli bir gericilik dönemine bırakan yeni bir tarihî safhaya girdiğine inanıyordu. Bu bakımdan Bakunin, Avrupa’nın geleceğini çağdaşlarının büyük çoğunluğundan çok daha isabetli değerlendirmişti. Yanıldığı nokta, bütün Avrupa’yı askerîleştiren bu yeni gericilik döneminin ne kadar süreceğine dair tahminiydi; lâkin mahiyetini kavramakta hiç kimse onun kadar isabetli değildi. Bunu, 11 Kasım 1874 tarihinde dostu Nikolay Ogaryov’a yazdığı dokunaklı mektupta açıkça görmek mümkündür:


“Bana gelince sevgili dostum, ben de bu defa nihayet bütün fiilî faaliyetlerden vazgeçtim ve aktif mücadeleyle olan bütün bağlarımı kopardım. Her şeyden önce, içinde bulunduğumuz zaman buna kesinlikle elverişli değildir. Bismarckçılık; yani militarizmin, polis idaresinin ve mali tekelin yeni devletçiliğe özgü tek bir sistem içinde birleşmiş hâli, her şeyi fethetmektedir. Belki de önümüzdeki on yahut on beş yıl boyunca insanlığa yönelmiş bu kudretli ve bilimsel inkâr hükmünü sürdürecektir. Bununla, bugün yapılacak hiçbir şey kalmadığını söylemek istemiyorum; lâkin yeni şartlar yeni yöntemler, her şeyden önce de taze kan gerektiriyor. Ben artık yeni mücadelelere elverişli olmadığımı hissediyorum ve yürekli Gil Blas’ın bana, ‘

Plus de homélies, Monseigneur

!’ [Artık vaaz yeter, Monsenyör!] demesini beklemeden görevimden çekiliyorum.”


Bakunin, adını bütün dünyaya duyuran iki büyük devrimci dönemin başlıca simalarından biri olmuştur. Max Nettlau’nun da belirttiği üzere, 1847 yılının Kasım ayında Polonya Devrimi’nin yıl dönümünde yaptığı cesur konuşmada yaklaşmakta olan fırtınayı önceden haber vermişti. Nitekim 1848 Şubat Devrimi Fransa’da patlak verdiğinde derhal Paris’e gitti ve devrimci hadiselerin tam ortasında, muhtemelen hayatının en mutlu haftalarını geçirdi. Lâkin kısa zamanda şunu da kavradı ki, Fransa’da zafere ulaşan devrim, Avrupa’nın dört bir yanında hissedilen isyan havası sebebiyle kaçınılmaz olarak başka ülkelere de yayılacak; bu sebeple bütün devrimci unsurları ortak bir hedef etrafında birleştirmek ve onların parçalanmasını önlemek hayati bir önem taşıyacaktı; zira böyle bir dağılmanın yalnızca pusuya yatmış karşıdevrime yarayacağını biliyordu.


Bakunin’in olayları önceden sezme kudreti, o dönemin genel devrimci ufkunun hayli ilerisindeydi. Bunu, Nisan 1848’de P. M. Annenkov’a yazdığı mektupta ve bilhassa aynı yılın Ağustos ayında Alman şairi dostu Georg Herwegh’e gönderdiği mektuplarda açıkça görmek mümkündür. Bununla birlikte, daha yüksek hedeflere yönelmeden önce mevcut şartların hesaba katılması ve büyük engellerin ortadan kaldırılması gerektiğini kavrayacak siyasî basirete de sahipti.


Berlin’deki Mart Devrimi’nin hemen ardından Bakunin Almanya’ya geçti. Buradaki amacı, Polonyalılar, Çekler ve diğer Slav halkları arasındaki çok sayıdaki dostuyla temas kurmak; onları Batı Avrupa ve Alman demokrasisiyle eşzamanlı olarak genel bir ayaklanmaya teşvik etmekti. Ona göre …

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Bakunin’in Siyaset Felsefesi – Orijinal Yayıncının Önsözü
content:
Çeviren: Scianus


FELSEFÎ ANARŞİZM son derece eski bir öğretidir. Hatta onun, yönetim fikri kadar eski olduğunu söylemek cazip gelebilir; ne var ki bunu kesin biçimde doğrulayacak açık kanıtlar elimizde mevcut değildir. Yine de iki bin yılı aşkın bir geçmişe sahip, yalnızca zorlayıcı iktidarın, cebrin ve bağlayıcı yasaların bulunmadığı bir toplum düzenini tasvir etmekle kalmayıp, böylesi bir toplumsal ilişki biçimini insanlığın ulaşması gereken ideal olarak gösteren metinlere sahibiz. Ovidius, anarşist ütopyayı son derece güzel ve şiirsel bir dille anlatır.

Dönüşümler

‘inin ilk kitabında, yasaların bulunmadığı altın çağı tasvir eder; öyle bir çağ ki, kimsenin zor kullanmasına ihtiyaç yoktur, zira herkes kendi iradesiyle sözünde durur ve doğru olanı yapar. Ceza korkusu yoktur; tunç levhalara kazınmış kanunlar bulunmaz; öç alacak bir hâkimin karşısında korkuyla bekleşen kalabalıklar görülmez. Yargıçlar olmaksızın herkes güven içinde yaşar. Romalı şairin tasavvuruyla modern felsefî anarşistlerin tasavvuru arasındaki tek fark, onun altın çağı insanlık tarihinin başlangıcına, onların ise sonuna yerleştirmeleridir.


Ne var ki bu düşüncelerin ilk mucidi Ovidius değildi. O, asırlardır yaşatılan fikirleri şiir diliyle yeniden dile getiriyordu. Alman toplum tarihçisi Georg Adler, 1899 yılında yayımladığı sosyalizm tarihine dair kapsamlı ve sağlam belgelere dayanan incelemesinde, Stoacı felsefenin kurucusu Zenon’un (MÖ 342-270) kesin olarak anarşist görüşlere sahip olduğunu göstermiştir.

1

 İlk dönem Hristiyan münzevilerinin birçoğunda da güçlü anarşist eğilimlerin bulunduğuna şüphe yoktur; hatta ikinci yüzyılda yaşamış Karpokrates ile takipçilerinin siyasî ve dinî görüşlerinde bu eğilimler belirgin, belki de baskın bir yer tutmaktadır. Bu anlayış, Orta Çağ boyunca bazı köktenci Hristiyan mezhepleri arasında, hatta modern döneme kadar yaşamaya devam etmiştir.


Anarşizmin yorulmak bilmez tarihçisi Max Nettlau da aynı sahayı incelemiş ve Fransız Devrimi’nden önceki iki yüzyıl içinde kaleme alınmış, güçlü liberter görüşler taşıyan yahut açıkça anarşist nitelik gösteren birçok eseri sıralamıştır.

2

 Bu dönemin en önemli Fransız eserleri arasında, yaklaşık 1550’de kaleme alınmasına rağmen ancak 1577’de yayımlanabilen Étienne de La Boétie’nin

Gönüllü Kulluk Üzerine Söylev

‘i; Gabriel Foigny’nin 1676’da isimsiz olarak yayımlanan

Les aventures de Jacques Sadeur dans la découverte et le voyage de la Terre Australe

 adlı eseri; Diderot’nun birkaç kısa denemesi; ayrıca Devrim’den hemen önceki yirmi yıl içinde yayımlanan Sylvain Maréchal’in şiirleri, fablları ve hikâyeleri sayılabilir. Aynı dönemde İngiltere’de de anarşist düşüncelerin izine rastlanır; tıpkı Fransa’da olduğu gibi burada da bu fikirler çoğunlukla yükselen burjuvazinin en radikal kanadının temsilcileri tarafından dile getirilmiştir. Nitekim Winstanley’nin bazı yazılarında anarşist görüşler açıkça görülür; ayrıca genç Burke’ün

Vindication of Natural Society

 (1756) adlı eserinde, her ne kadar amacı hiciv yapmak olsa da, anarşi lehine son derece ustalıklı bir muhakeme geliştirdiği de iyi bilinmektedir.


Bununla birlikte, bu erken döneme ait bütün bu eserler ve daha niceleri, onları sonraki anarşist literatürden köklü biçimde ayıran iki temel özellikten en az birini taşırlar. Bunlar ya Foigny ile Maréchal’in eserlerinde olduğu gibi açıkça ütopyacı metinlerdir ya da bir hükümdarın yahut hükümetin yol açtığı somut bir haksızlığa karşı kaleme alınmış, belirli bir siyasî durumda daha geniş bir hareket serbestîsi elde etmeyi amaçlayan siyasî broşürlerdir. Çoğu zaman siyaset teorisine dair tartışmalara da yer verirler; ancak bunlar tali mahiyettedir ve eserin asıl gayesini teşkil etmez.


Sistematik bir öğreti olarak felsefî anarşizmin başlangıcı, genel kabul gören görüşe göre, İngiltere’de William Godwin’in 1793 yılında yayımlanan

Enquiry Concerning Political Justice

 adlı eserine kadar götürülebilir. Godwin’in anarşizmi de, ondan hemen önce gelen düşünürlerin ve yaklaşık elli yıl sonra Proudhon’un geliştirdiği anarşizm de, küçük burjuvazinin en radikal kesiminin siyaset teorisini ifade eder. 1688 İngiliz Devrimi ile 1789 Fransız Devrimi’nde burjuvazi, daha önce siyasî iktidarı tekellerinde bulunduran taç ile aristokrasinin bu ayrıcalığını kırmıştı. Devrim sonrasındaki hükümetler, uzun süre toprak aristokrasisinin ve bürokrasinin, ki uzun müddet

noblesse de robe

 niteliğini korumuştu, güçlü tesiri altında kalmaya devam ettiler. Bununla birlikte, giderek güçlenen …

author: Unknown
title: Two commanders in the footsteps of Egîd
content:
After centuries of a period of unwritten history in Kurdistan, the colonial policy based on partition and denial-annihilation that was developed over the last century led to a process that suppressed, distorted and destroyed all the social characteristics and qualities of the Kurdish people, both culturally and sociologically. The Kurdish people, one of the oldest peoples of Mesopotamia, are a community that took shape and developed its culture in a geography that was the cradle of the Neolithic Revolution. For this reason, the policies of denial and genocide imposed on Kurdish society, with its profound social richness, and all colonial attacks seeking to achieve their aims through physical and white genocide have failed to reach their intended result, colliding with the rich traditions and cultural wall of the Kurdish people rooted deep in history. Of course, the multifaceted and deepened assimilation developed on this basis achieved certain results and caused enormous social destruction, but it failed to annihilate the people completely.


With the spread and acceptance, particularly among the youth of Kurdistan, of the ideological and political line created and developed by Leader Apo, who emerged on the stage of history in the last quarter of the twentieth century, and with the process of party-building, mass mobilisation and resistance that developed on this basis, all the characteristics, abilities and qualities that had been suppressed for centuries and remained hidden within Kurdish society were brought to light through this developing resistance process. On this basis, as Kurdish society was revitalised, many of its social and cultural characteristics erupted almost like a volcano during the Revolution of Resurrection, revitalising society; and the social reality that had stood on the edge of an abyss, on this basis, almost grew wings, experiencing a rebirth and reconnecting with the traditional characteristics rooted in the richness of history, while developing the process of nationalisation on this basis.


The heroes of Maraş against colonialism


One of the areas where this Apoist emergence first found a response and created an echo was Maraş, a city on the Anatolian border of Kurdistan. Pazarcık was one of the first places where our movement found a mass base as it was being brought into Kurdistan. Pazarcık, Elbistan and Maraş as a whole, as well as Malatya, Adıyaman, Dêrsim and all the areas along the border region, were among those most exposed to colonialist, genocidal and assimilationist attacks. Our movement initially focused heavily on these areas, and the necessary social response was soon given along this line as well. On this basis, the people of the region embraced and joined the Apoist thought as a stance against assimilation and dissolution. This was, in fact, a stance of existence and resistance against annihilation. The revolutionary movement that developed on this basis reached a significant base in the area, particularly in Pazarcık, and experienced its first mass mobilisation there.


The Maraş Massacre taking place at a time when revolutionary activity was on the rise to such an extent that even villages were being given names such as Vietnam was certainly no coincidence; it was an organised and planned colonial policy. The fascist coup of 12 September that followed immediately afterwards is clear evidence of this. All of this was developed as a major wave of attacks aimed at preventing the developing revolutionary struggle and suppressing the patriotic revolutionary movement that was rapidly growing in the region. From then on, repression and attacks intensified, the policy of forced displacement was deepened, and an attempt was made, so to speak, to cleanse the region of Kurds. Yet the people of the region did not give up. Wherever they went, they supported and took the lead in revolutionary and patriotic activities.


We know very well that these areas also provided the ground for the initial process of cadre formation and militantisation of our movement, through the efforts of the great internationalist revolutionaries, comrades Haki Karer and Kemal Pir. This was a period in which pioneering and courageous cadres such as Erdal (Mustafa Yöndem), Besê Anuş, Cin Ali (Ali Erek), Sarı Ömer (Mustafa Ömürcan), Sabri (Şıho Dirlik), Kasım Engin (İsmail Nazlıkul), Erdal (Engin Sincer), Nucan (Cennet Dirlik), Atakan Mahir (İbrahim Çoban), Savaş Maraş (Mehmet Soysüren) and Berfin Nurhak …

author: Unknown
title: TJK-E: We stand with Afghan women
content:
The European Kurdish Women’s Movement (TJK-E), in a statement expressing solidarity with Afghan women, said in a statement: "Five years have passed since the Taliban seized power in Afghanistan once again on 15 August 2021. During this period, repression, bans and restrictions against women have steadily intensified. Women have been excluded from education and working life and pushed out of political, social and public life.


The erasure of women from the public sphere is not only a violation of fundamental rights and freedoms; it is also a systematic policy that leaves women more vulnerable to violence, repression, torture and all forms of attack. This mentality, which denies women’s will, identity and right to life, is one of the most extreme forms of male-dominated and patriarchal thinking."


The statement underlined that "the war in Afghanistan, launched after the 11 September attacks under the banner of ‘democracy and freedom’, affected the lives of millions of people for twenty years. The Taliban’s return to power following the withdrawal of the US and other Western powers from Afghanistan in 2021, and the abandonment of Afghan women’s future to the mercy of this repressive regime, has been one of the grave consequences of interest-driven war policies.


It is unacceptable to remain silent today in the face of the deprivation of Afghan women’s fundamental rights. The international community must not ignore the systematic violations of women’s rights by the Taliban authorities and must not contribute to the normalisation of a system in which women are excluded, and fundamental freedoms are denied."


The statement added: "Despite all the repression, Afghan women continue to resist. The struggle of Afghan women who refuse to give up their right to education, work, political participation and a free life is part of the struggle for women’s freedom around the world.


For this reason, we support the freedom campaign that will begin on 15 August and continue until 25 November. As Kurdish women in Europe, we once again express our solidarity with Afghan women and declare that we do not see their struggle as separate from our own struggle for freedom.


Women’s solidarity is a common force that transcends borders.


As women’s common struggle against the male-dominated, statist and patriarchal mentality grows, so too will the possibilities for social liberation. Because society cannot be free without the liberation of women; where women’s will is not recognised, there can be no democratic society.


Transforming the 21st century into a century of women’s freedom, and creating free women and a free society together, is our common struggle."

author: Brian Hioe
title: KMT Reverses Course on Drones, Passes Caning Referendum
content:
THE KMT HAS passed a 44.2 billion NT six-year budget for drone funding, as well as 19.2 billion NT in procurement for Executive Yuan agencies. This takes place as part of the passage of the overall budget of 2.9869 trillion NT, which was held up for 266 days.

This is a reversal for the KMT, which shortly before planned to cut all such funding or to freeze it. Nevertheless, the KMT’s approval of drone funding places this under the central government budget, rather than as a special budget.

The KMT seemed to have suddenly become aware of the poor optics of blocking drone spending after an article in The Economist, which lashed out at the KMT as obstructionist and self-interested for continuing to block drone spending when this could be vital to Taiwan’s defense against Chinese threats. Afterward, the KMT legislative caucus suddenly had a reversal of course.

Splits in the KMT are increasingly visible. KMT Legislative Yuan president Han Kuo-yu recently lashed out at KMT legislative caucus leader Fu Kun-chi for failing to appear at cross-party negotiations about the budget, and not authorizing his deputy, Lin Pei-hsiang, to conduct negotiations on their behalf. Han suggested that Fu could resign as caucus chair if he continued to stymie budget discussions. Han may be aiming to differentiate his political stance from Fu, with some suspecting that Han may have his eyes on running again for president in 2028–this time as a moderate, in contrast to Fu and KMT chair Cheng Li-wun.

Yet it is possible that the KMT does not actually intend to change course on drone funding, just to present the optics of having changed course. For one, while Han criticized Fu publicly, as Legislative Yuan president or as a high-ranking KMT official, he could have taken more severe measures against Fu intended to force compliance. Han’s actions may only be for show. It is to be seen whether efforts to stymie drone programs later take place, as there are other means of accomplishing this. The KMT does not have any good explanation as to why they held up the drone budget for so long before changing abruptly on the matter.

In the meantime, yesterday the KMT also pushed through three referendums: on nuclear energy, caning, and using traffic fines as budget for road safety improvements by local governments. A referendum on the issue of euthanasia proposed by the TPP was rejected, on the basis of lack of adequate social discussion or consensus on the issue–probably not incorrect, seeing as the idea was proposed late by the TPP. It is unknown how relations between the two parties stand after splitting on the issue, though it was never a core issue for the TPP, and one introduced late as a means of having a distinctive campaign platform.

With regard to a referendum on nuclear energy, calling for the abolishment of policies for a nuclear-free homeland, the KMT would again be attempting to leverage on a traditional partisan issue with its base. That being said, the Lai administration has already reversed course on the issue of nuclear restarts, submitting plans for the restart of two reactors, which might undercut the KMT.

As for the referendum on caning, caning is proposed by the KMT as punishment for severe crimes such as sexual assault, large-scale fraud, and child abuse. The referendum is likely to be mocked now that there is more widespread discussion of the idea. Still, one notes that though KMT chair Cheng Li-wun seemed to be in favor of dropping the idea, this met with pushback within the KMT, and it remained on the ballot. Even as drones may be vital for Taiwan’s future in the face of threats, the KMT remained more consistently committed to the idea of a caning referendum.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Court asked again to recognize Ampatuan massacre’s 58th victim
content:
“As the years pass, it becomes easier for the world to move on. But for the families left behind, there is no moving on.”

CAGAYAN DE ORO — The daughter of Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay, one of the slain journalists and media workers in the 2009 Ampatuan massacre, asked again the Court of Appeals (CA) to judicially recognize her father as the 58th victim.

Maria Reynafe Momay-Castillo, together with her legal counsel, filed the manifestation with reiterative motion before the appellate court in Manila on August 14, expressing her persistent hope to achieve justice.

“As the years pass, it becomes easier for the world to move on. But for the families left behind, there is no moving on. There is only learning how to carry the loss while continuing to hope that their lives will never be forgotten,” Momay-Castillo said in her manifestation.

Read: Justice still elusive after 16 years of Ampatuan massacre

Her father whose remains have never been recovered was a photojournalist for the Midland Review.

The family stressed that he was one of the 32 journalists and media workers who were part of the convoy, together with the family of Esmael “Toto” Mangudadatu, to cover the latter’s certificate of candidacy for the 2010 gubernatorial elections.

On November 23, 2009, 58 individuals, including family members of Mangudadatu, two lawyers, and motorists who passed the same route, were killed after they were ambushed while traveling to Shariff Aguak, Maguindanao (now Maguindanao del Sur). The victims were buried in mass graves in Sitio Masalay, Barangay Salman, Ampatuan town.

In its consolidated partial decision dated December 19, 2019, the Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 221 ruled that the prosecution failed to sufficiently establish the death of Momay. This explains why only 57 counts of murder were imposed on the convicted individuals, and Momay’s heirs were not granted any compensation for damages.

The court said that the prosecution only established that Momay could no longer be found after he was seen with the convoy on November 23, 2009. It said that his death could not be ascertained since no cadaver was found and no death certificate was presented.

Authorities recovered a partial upper denture in the crime scene eight days after the massacre. It reportedly belonged to Momay. The victim’s live-in partner for 22 years testified that it was the same denture she cleaned every night. A certain missionary also confirmed to investigators that he was the one who made the denture because of the special marking.

The court, however, ruled that their testimonies did not sufficiently establish that it belonged to the photojournalist. “Ergo, this court concludes that the first element of murder – ‘that a person was killed’ – is absent in this case. The 58th count of murder will not prosper for it lacks corpus delicti.”

The family stressed that the brutal incident still causes strong pain, as they have no closure due to Momay’s unrecovered remains. They urged the appellate court to reconsider its December 2019 decision.

“It reminds us that justice is not only about court decisions. Justice is also about remembering. It is about refusing to let history fade into silence. It is about ensuring that future generations know what happened and why it should never happen again,” Momay-Castillo said.

For the family and lawyers, the non-recognition of Momay as a victim is “a profound failure” that demands urgent rectification.

Almost 17 years have passed since the gruesome incident but full justice remains elusive, as only 44 individuals, including prominent members of the Ampatuan clan, were convicted. Many of the accused remain at large.

Last year, the Center for International Law (CenterLaw) Philippines, which handles the case of 19 victims, including Momay, filed a motion asking the CA to resolve their consolidated appeals without further delay. Lawyer Gilbert Andres, CenterLaw Philippines executive director, told Bulatlat that they have yet to receive any update.

“The passage of time—now moving towards 17 years—cannot diminish the Philippine State’s obligations to ensure accountability for grave human rights violations,” the manifestation stated. (DAA)

author: Unknown
title: Pezeşkiyan: Sorunumuz kat kat arttı, gelirimiz de azaldı
content:
İran Cumhurbaşkanı Mesud Pezeşkiyan, ABD ve İsrail’le yaşanan savaşın ardından ülke ekonomisindeki sorunların daha da ağırlaştığını söyledi.

İran basınında yer alan haberlere göre bir toplantıda konuşan Pezeşkiyan, ithal ürünlerin geçmişte daha doğrudan güzergâhlardan ülkeye ulaştırıldığını, bugün ise farklı yollar üzerinden İran’a sokulabildiğini belirtti.

Pezeşkiyan, ulaşım ve tedarik süreçlerinin uzamasının ürünlerin maliyetini artırdığını ve bunun fiyatlara yansıdığını ifade etti.

İran Cumhurbaşkanı, ekonomik sorunların önemli nedenlerinden birinin de devlet gelirlerindeki düşüş olduğunu söyledi.

Petrol gelirlerine işaret eden Pezeşkiyan, “Bizim gelirimiz de azaldı. Eskiden petrol satıyorduk, şimdi satamıyoruz.” dedi.

Gelirlerin azalmasına karşın devletin ekonomik yükünün arttığını belirten Pezeşkiyan, savaşın ülke ekonomisi üzerindeki etkilerine dikkat çekti.

Pezeşkiyan, ABD ve İsrail saldırılarında çok sayıda sanayi tesisinin zarar gördüğünü belirterek, bunun vergi gelirlerinde de düşüşe yol açtığını söyledi.

“Bir sürü fabrikayı vurdular ve tahrip ettiler.” diyen Pezeşkiyan, zarar gören işletmelerden vergi toplanamadığını, aksine bu işletmelerin ayakta kalabilmesi için devlet desteğine ihtiyaç duyduğunu ifade etti.

Pezeşkiyan, “Fabrikalardan vergi de toplayamıyoruz, sadece o da değil, üstüne onlara para da vermek zorundayız ki ayakta kalabilsinler.” diye konuştu.

İran Cumhurbaşkanı, savaşın ardından ekonomik sorunların geçmişe kıyasla çok daha ağır hale geldiğini belirterek mevcut durumu, “Sorunumuz kat kat arttı ve gelirimiz de azaldı.” sözleriyle özetledi.

Pezeşkiyan’ın açıklamaları, savaşın İran ekonomisinde üretim, dış ticaret, petrol gelirleri ve kamu maliyesi üzerindeki etkilerine ilişkin hükümetin değerlendirmelerini ortaya koydu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Putin: Rusya-Kuzey Kore ilişkileri benzeri görülmemiş seviyeye ulaştı
content:
Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin, Kuzey Kore’nin Japon sömürge yönetiminden kurtuluşunun yıl dönümü dolayısıyla Kuzey Kore lideri Kim Jong-un’a kutlama mesajı gönderdi.

Kremlin’in yayımladığı mesajda Putin, 15 Ağustos’un Kore halkının Japon sömürge yönetiminden kurtuluşunu simgelediğini belirterek, bu süreçte Koreli yurtseverler ile Kızıl Ordu askerlerinin birlikte mücadele ettiğini ifade etti.

Putin, iki ülke arasındaki ilişkilerin tarihsel olarak bu dönemde oluşan “savaş kardeşliği” ve karşılıklı dayanışma geleneklerine dayandığını kaydetti.

Putin, mesajında Rusya ile Kuzey Kore arasındaki mevcut ilişkilerin geldiği noktaya dikkat çekti.

Putin, “Bugün Moskova ile Pyongyang arasındaki ilişkiler, kapsamlı stratejik ortaklık bakımından benzeri görülmemiş yüksek bir seviyeye ulaştı” ifadelerini kullandı.

İki ülkenin bugün farklı alanlarda iş birliğini sürdürdüğünü belirten Putin, Moskova ve Pyongyang’ın bölgesel güvenlik ve istikrarın sağlanması konusunda da koordinasyon içinde olduğunu söyledi.

Rus lider, Rusya ve Kuzey Kore’nin hem ikili ilişkilerde hem de uluslararası gündemde ortak çalışmalarını sürdüreceğini belirtti.

Putin, bu iş birliğinin iki ülke halklarının çıkarlarına hizmet etmesinin yanı sıra “daha adil ve gerçek demokratik bir dünya düzeninin” kurulmasına katkı sağlayacağı görüşünü dile getirdi.

Moskova ile Pyongyang arasındaki ilişkiler özellikle son dönemde siyasi, ekonomik ve askeri alanlarda daha da yakınlaştı. İki ülke arasındaki stratejik ortaklık, Ukrayna savaşı ve Asya-Pasifik bölgesindeki güvenlik dengeleri açısından da uluslararası siyasetin önemli başlıklarından biri haline geldi.

author: Kevin Damásio
title: Quase quatro a cada dez indígenas em terras na Amazônia não têm acesso adequado a água
content:
Um igarapé na região do Lago do Boto, na Terra Indígena (TI) Munduruku, marcou a infância de Ediene Kirixi. Era ali que ela bebia água, pescava e se banhava desde o final dos anos 80. Na segunda metade da década de 90, o garimpo ilegal de ouro nas cabeceiras do Alto Rio Tapajós, no sudoeste do Pará, contaminou os corpos hídricos do entorno da sua aldeia. Em 1997, Ediene, na época com 10 anos, teve que se mudar com a família e se instalou na beira do Tapajós, cujas águas ainda estavam limpas. Até que, a partir de 2018, o avanço da exploração mineral ganhou intensidade na bacia e transformou de vez o que restava do rio cristalino na região.


“Hoje, as nossas crianças já não têm mais a liberdade de tomar a água do rio. A cor do rio é branca, os peixes estão doentes. A água desce com as sujeiras e chega até nós. Isso deixa muitas aldeias sem ter o que beber”, observa Ediene, 39 anos, coordenadora da Associação das Mulheres Munduruku Wakoborũn, que representa sete territórios indígenas da bacia do Tapajós.


Hoje, as nossas crianças já não têm mais a liberdade de tomar a água do rio. A cor do rio é branca, os peixes estão doentes. A água desce com as sujeiras e chega até nós. Isso deixa muitas aldeias sem ter o que beber.


Ediene Kirixi


Coordenadora da Associação das Mulheres Munduruku Wakoborũn, que representa sete territórios indígenas da bacia do Tapajós


A degradação dos corpos hídricos por atividades como garimpo e desmatamento, agravada pela ocorrência mais frequente e intensa de eventos climáticos extremos, aumenta os riscos para quem depende dessas águas. Análise da InfoAmazonia, com base em dados do Censo Demográfico de 2022, do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), mostra que quase 40% da população indígena em terras indígenas na Amazônia Legal não tem acesso adequado à água e, por isso, depende principalmente de rios, lagos e igarapés para obtê-la. O saneamento básico, que deveria garantir o acesso seguro à água e outros serviços essenciais como esgotamento sanitário e destinação adequada do lixo, ainda é precário nessas comunidades.


Na Amazônia Legal, 116 mil moradores de terras indígenas (27,38% do total da população indígena em TIs) estão conectados à rede geral de distribuição, enquanto 145 mil (34,29%) captam água sobretudo de poços, fontes, nascentes ou minas. Essas formas de abastecimento

são consideradas oficialmente adequadas e mais seguras

 por contarem, em geral, com canalização, fornecimento contínuo, quantidade suficiente e garantia de potabilidade.


Entre as demais formas de acesso à água, 114 mil pessoas (27%) dependem principalmente de rios, lagos e igarapés para obter água. Há, ainda, 37 mil indígenas (8,71%) que coletam água da chuva, 5.067 (1,19%) dependem de carro-pipa e 5.924 (1,4%) obtêm o recurso de formas não especificadas nas terras indígenas da Amazônia Legal.


A população que vive na maior bacia hidrográfica de água doce do mundo sofre de estresse hídrico


Caetano Scannavino


Coordenador-geral do Projeto Saúde e Alegria


“A população que vive na maior bacia hidrográfica de água doce do mundo sofre de estresse hídrico. A água dos rios não é a mesma de 100 anos atrás. Boa parte é de baixa qualidade, contaminada”, diz Caetano Scannavino, coordenador-geral do Projeto Saúde e Alegria.


Desde 1987, a organização fornece serviços de saúde e saneamento básico para povos indígenas e tradicionais da bacia do Tapajós. Nas terras indígenas da região, apenas 20% dos domicílios contam com poço, fonte, nascente ou mina; 43% estão conectados à rede geral de distribuição de água; e 35% ainda dependem principalmente de rios, lagos e igarapés.


Na Terra Indígena Munduruku, esse percentual é ainda maior: quase 40% dos 9.281 habitantes têm nos corpos hídricos sua principal fonte de água, e as aldeias com acesso a poço, fonte, nascente ou mina, como a Kaba Rewûn, onde Ediene vive, abrangem apenas 2 mil pessoas (22%).


“O garimpo deixou um rastro, derrubando os pés de açaí, buriti, patauá, e falta caça. Com a estiagem de 2023, os igarapés secaram fora do normal e foram acabando com os peixes. As aldeias ficaram sem ter o que comer”, observa Ediene. “Várias sobrevivem da água de igarapés contaminados pelo mercúrio e precisam de poço. A nossa luta agora é cobrar o governo a fazer instalações de água nas aldeias onde ainda não tem”.
